# SerpApi Hacktoberfest 2026 Resources

A collection of SerpApi tutorials, livestream resources, and runnable demos for Hacktoberfest 2026\. Use them to build AI agents that work with live web data.

## Join the Hacktoberfest DEV Challenges

Building something with SerpApi? Submit it to the **Best Use of SerpApi** category in the Hacktoberfest DEV Challenges. Give an agent live search, ground its answers in current sources, or build something useful with search data.

Choose the current challenge and theme from the hub, build a new project with open-source AI at its core, and publish your entry using that challenge's submission template. Show your demo, explain how you used SerpApi, and tell readers why open innovation matters for your project. Check the challenge page for its deadline and rules. **We'd love to see what you build. Submit your project on DEV!**

## Livestream Resources

For the SerpApi livestream, Making Open Models Smarter with Tools, MCP, and Skills, use these resources to follow along and keep building:

The livestream slides are available here.

| Resource                                                                                                                           | What you'll learn or find                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Building an AI Agent in Python](https://serpapi.com/blog/building-an-ai-agent-in-python/)                                         | A walkthrough of models, tools, memory, context, and the agent loop.                     |
| [How to Fit More Web Search Data into a Local LLM](https://serpapi.com/blog/local-llm-web-search-markdown-output/)                 | Use Markdown output and JSON Restrictor to reduce the search data sent to a local model. |
| [How to Connect Your Local LLM with Web Search Data](https://serpapi.com/blog/how-to-connect-your-local-llm-with-web-search-data/) | Connect a locally running model to live search results.                                  |
| [Introducing SerpApi's New Markdown Output](https://serpapi.com/blog/introducing-serpapi-markdown-output/)                         | Request search results in Markdown for use with LLMs and agents.                         |
| [Local LLM Web Search: source code](https://github.com/serpapi/local-llm-web-search)                                               | The example app for connecting a local LLM to SerpApi through function calling.          |

## SerpApi for Agents

* SerpApi MCP: Connect agents to live search through Model Context Protocol.
* SerpApi CLI: Access SerpApi from the command line.
* SerpApi Skill: Give agents guidance on using SerpApi.
* SerpApi Search Tools package: Add search tools to Python agent frameworks.
* SerpApi llms.txt: Find API documentation in a format agents can read.

## Run the Demos

This repository also includes three small livestream demos. Follow the setup and run instructions to run them with uv and a local model in LM Studio:

| Demo                                                                                | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [MCP demo](/serpapi/hacktoberfest-2026/blob/main/demo%5Fagents/mcp%5Fdemo.py)       | Live web searches and stock quotes through SerpApi MCP.                                                                                                                            |
| [CLI demo](/serpapi/hacktoberfest-2026/blob/main/demo%5Fagents/cli%5Fdemo.py)       | An agent running uv commands to inspect Python and installed packages.                                                                                                             |
| [Skills demo](/serpapi/hacktoberfest-2026/blob/main/demo%5Fagents/skills%5Fdemo.py) | An agent loading the [SerpApi page extraction skill](/serpapi/hacktoberfest-2026/blob/main/demo%5Fagents/skills/serpapi-page-extract/SKILL.md) to retrieve a web page as Markdown. |

input.overview: Validate Week 3 as a local handoff writer for 3D artists — not an in-DCC chatbot — using a Temporal harness, one documentation skill, and local Gemma. Copy the week 2 master-file pattern into a new repo, and leave every other sponsor out.
input.plan:
# Shot Note — Week 3 idea lock

## The decision

Keep both instincts, and give them different jobs.

- **Constraint, not a product:** a tool for 3D artists that is not another chat panel inside Blender, Houdini, or Maya. An in-DCC agent with skills already exists in the wild (a Blender add-on whose agent half is a chat that sees the scene). That is the shape to stay away from.
- **Product:** a documentation wizard that **writes the page you owe after the pass**, from an export that already sits on disk. The dreaded task is the handoff, not hunting the manual. A wizard that answers “what does this node do?” is a chatbot with search, and it would pull in SerpApi or Browserbase for a job this theme does not need.

**Working name: Shot Note.** You can rename the folder before the first push. One sentence: after a lookdev or lighting pass, drop the scene export you already have, and Shot Note writes the one-page handoff, then waits for you to approve it so you can get back to the viewport.

**Lazy payoff to measure before the post:** minutes to write that page by hand from a fixed sample export, versus minutes to review the generated page. The announcement’s optional section is exactly this number. Posts that admit they never timed it leave the strongest judging hook empty.

Theme source: [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 3](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week3-2026-10-19) (event 81), announced in [Slow and Steady](https://dev.to/devteam/join-the-hacktoberfest-open-source-ai-challenge-slow-and-steady-2850-in-prizes-across-21-3iee). Active now. Written deadline **Sunday, October 25, 11:59 PM PDT**. The API `ends_at` is `2026-10-25T06:59:00.000Z`, which is **Saturday, October 24, 11:59 PM PDT**. Week 2’s prose matched its API timestamp; this week’s prose is a day later than the timestamp. Build so a judge can run it Saturday night.

Open-source AI has to be what makes it work: local open-weight Gemma writes the page; the harness only keeps that job alive. Scene paths and texture notes stay on the machine. That is the open-innovation paragraph: a closed API would upload the shot.

## What winners did that Week 2 did not

From the [Touch Grass winners roundup](https://dev.to/devteam/congrats-to-the-hacktoberfest-open-source-ai-challenge-touch-grass-winners-152c) (that challenge is over; this is style, not a place to submit):

- The title is the moment, not the stack. Paper Trail is “Gemma writes your walk a field card, then the screen goes away,” and it is a 6-minute read. The post judges reacted to most led with a measured number (28 of 33 alerts).
- Your Week 1 Mastra win was a 20-minute post and took a partner category. Writing quality is weighted first again this week. Aim for a short post: one person, one dreaded page, one clocked before/after, one diagram.
- Enter only categories the demo actually exercises. A current Week 3 entry that only claims Gemma, and says so, is the right instinct. Win once. A longer sponsor list does not add prize money.

Week 3 submissions already cluster on local models that tidy inboxes, Downloads folders, and task lists. A DCC handoff is not in that pile.

## Stack: two tools, because each one does a different job

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  exportFile[SceneExportOnDisk] --> readFile[HarnessCallbackReadsLocalFile]
  readFile --> skill[ShotHandoffSkill]
  skill --> gemma[LocalGemma]
  gemma --> draft[MarkdownHandoff]
  draft --> approval[ArtistApproves]
  approval --> page[FinishedPage]
```

- **Brain — Gemma, local (featured).** The model fills the handoff. Ollama, a small Gemma the machine already runs. Featured category only if the golden path shows Gemma output, not a template pretending to be a model. Week 2’s brief was honest that templates wrote the listing; this week the model has to write the page, or there is no Gemma story.
- **Harness — Temporal Agent Harness (partner).** It earns the category with capabilities the product uses: a callback tool reads the export on the laptop, the model call retries as an activity, and the built-in approval gate pauses until you accept the page. Crash and resume is the sloth behavior: start the note, walk away, come back to the same draft. Pin `temporal-agent-harness==0.7.0`. The repo’s own README marks LangGraph support inside the harness as planned, not shipped, so do not combine this with the [LangGraph plugin](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/python/integrations/langgraph).
- **Skill — one file, `skills/shot-handoff/SKILL.md`.** This is product knowledge, the same idea as the SerpApi skills demo you watched, not an MLH sponsor bundle. The skill fixes the page: shot, DCC and version, what changed, materials and color spaces, render settings, known issues, evidence, what the next person must not change. The model is not allowed to freestyle a chat reply. That structure matches how a useful studio handoff is actually written: outcome, boundary, and evidence.

**Friday time-box.** The harness wants four local processes (Temporal dev server, session-manager, UI, worker) and its model plugins are Gemini, OpenAI Agents, and Pydantic AI. Local Gemma fits only if Pydantic AI can point at Ollama’s OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If that is not up Friday night, drop to the Temporal Python SDK: one workflow, the same skill, the same Ollama call, the same approval pause. That is still an honest Temporal entry. Do not spend the weekend on the experimental UI.

**Leave out, on purpose.** SerpApi and Browserbase answer live docs, which is the rejected chatbot. Mastra would be a second harness (Week 2 registered it and never ran the agent loop). Sentry duplicates the harness event stream. Render, DigitalOcean, Tiger, Atlas, Auth0, ElevenLabs, TabPFN, Tinker, Arduino, Ultramarine, and a `.tech` domain do not do a job this page needs. No credits get claimed while planning; the promo page is [hacktoberfest.com/my](https://hacktoberfest.com/my) if a later host decision needs one.

Surface if both tools show up in the demo: overall $250 + Gemma $200 + Temporal $100. Take-home is one prize. The post is the contest.

## Golden path (under a minute for a judge)

1. A checked-in sample export, plain text, so nobody needs Blender installed. A real personal export can replace it later.
2. Start the workflow. The skill is the only instruction set.
3. Gemma returns a markdown handoff. The run pauses on the approval step.
4. Approve. The page is the demo. Record the hand-written time next to it.

No DCC plugin. No second model call. No search.

## What carries over from Week 2

New folder, sibling of price-wire, not inside it. You name it before `git init` and the first push. Suggested folder: `d:\Documents\vscode\shot-note`.

Copy the **pattern** from [price-wire/hacktoberfest-week2](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2), with Week 3 facts filled in and Price Wire specifics deleted:

- [SIDE-HUSTLE-CHEATSHEET.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\SIDE-HUSTLE-CHEATSHEET.md) becomes `SLOW-AND-STEADY-CHEATSHEET.md`: one tool per slot, the stops (new repo inside the window, one English post, tags `devchallenge` and `hf26challenge`), and the card (payer, open brain, why closed loses, featured, partners, dropped).
- [VIABILITY-STUDY.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\VIABILITY-STUDY.md) becomes the decision record above, including the rejected manual-reader and the rejected in-DCC chat.
- [POSITIONING.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\POSITIONING.md), [PRODUCT-BRIEF.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\PRODUCT-BRIEF.md), and [WALKTHROUGH.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\WALKTHROUGH.md) stay as the one-page story, the honest implemented-versus-not list, and the judge path.
- [DEVRELAY-SESSION.md](d:\Documents\vscode\price-wire\hacktoberfest-week2\DEVRELAY-SESSION.md) is the rule to keep: **one session id**. Week 2 split 889 and 899. Do not reuse 899.

DevRelay’s CLI submits a transcript (`devrelay sessions submit --title "..." --file transcript.json`). It does not open a live logger. This chat is the log. Submit once after the first build slice, store that id, and update the same session. Submission sections, from the announcement template: What I Built, Demo, Code, How I Built It, Why Does Open Innovation Matter, optional My Agent Session, optional The Lazy Payoff, Prize Categories.

Do not copy Serp, TabPFN, Mastra, Tiger, listing templates, or the Price Wire deploy story.

## After you approve

1. You pick the folder name. Create it, add the five master files, no product code yet.
2. Build the skill, the sample export, and the Temporal workflow against local Gemma, with the Friday fallback written in the cheatsheet.
3. Time the handoff. Fill the walkthrough. Outline the post. Do not publish until you say so.

# Week 3 — in-pipeline documentation wizard

## What changed

The handoff writer is dropped. It described a page a lead or a future artist would read after a pass. You have not used that page, so it is not a pain this project can claim.

The requirement that replaces it: the tool runs **inside the DCC**, or on the open file as a **pipeline step**. A folder you drop an export into, with no scene and no operator, does not qualify.

Still in force: it is a documentation wizard, and the interface is not a chat box. The thing selected in the scene, or the step of the ritual, is the question.

Working name stays unset until the job is picked. Folder is a new sibling of price-wire. You name it before the first push.

## The job is still open

Both shapes below are documentation wizards, both sit on the scene, and both refuse a chatbot. They are different products.

**A. Manual for the selection.** You pick a node, modifier, or parameter. The wizard returns the official section for this software version and that control, inside the app. The pain is leaving the viewport, searching, and landing on the wrong version or a forum post. SerpApi’s markdown output is the live page. A skill tells the model how this DCC’s docs are structured and which version string to send. Gemma cuts the page down to the lines that apply. Temporal is a weak fit: one lookup does not need a durable harness. Use Temporal here only if the lookup retries and then offers to apply a documented setting, with your approval before the scene changes.

**B. One pipeline ritual you already repeat.** Name one multi-step job you redo by hand because the docs are long (publish, bake, material cleanup, export prep). The skill is that procedure, in order, with stop conditions. The DCC operators are the tools. Gemma is called only when the scene does not match the next step. Temporal earns the category: each operator is an activity, a failed bake resumes, and a destructive step waits for approval. SerpApi stays out unless one step truly depends on a current doc page. This is the stack you asked for (harness, skill, local model) used for real.

A is closer to the words “documentation wizard.” B is closer to “part of the pipeline” and to a harness that is doing work. The plan locks one of them after you answer. It will not invent a third job.

Deadline is unchanged. [Week 3](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week3-2026-10-19) (event 81), announced in [Slow and Steady](https://dev.to/devteam/join-the-hacktoberfest-open-source-ai-challenge-slow-and-steady-2850-in-prizes-across-21-3iee). That is a pipeline tool. A shelf button or Python panel runs on the open hip. The same resolver can run as a hython preflight on a hip in the publish step and print the doc line for each selected node. A folder you drop a text file into is not the product.

## Why this is the pain, and why the model stays small

Houdini help is a full page in another window. The page is often right and still slow to use: the goal of the paragraph is buried, one step hides three actions, and a warning sits under the command you were about to run. The wizard puts the matching section in the network editor and leads with the version and the parameter name.

The skill’s first rule is version: `hou.applicationVersion()` goes out with the node type. The reply cites the page URL. If the fetched page is for a different build, the wizard says so and stops. # Houdini documentation wizard — Week 3

## Why this, next to the help you already have

Houdini’s node help (the `?` on the node, or the help shortcut) already opens the right page for that node, from the build you installed. A menu in another DCC opens the whole manual, and you go find the page. A tool that only shows a shorter copy of that page does not earn a shelf button. People will keep opening the real help.

The wizard is the page turned into a short pass over the node you have selected.

- The help page is a document you read.
- The wizard is one documented check at a time, compared with the parameters already on the node, waiting for your answer before anything changes.

You still decide the path, the count, the look, and when to cook. The heavy lifting is reading a long page down to the few rules that bite, and noticing that the node in front of you already breaks one of them. That is the hour artists lose after a cache, a sim, or an export, not while they are choosing the art.

You get faster at the node because each step shows the sentence from the help before the question. The tool never finishes the setup behind you. Next time, the sentence is yours.

## One pass, so the version line is obvious

Demo story, unless you name a node you actually reopen help for: a **File Cache** SOP.

You select it and click the shelf tool. Three screens, then you stop.

1. Help says to turn on **Load from Disk** only after a file exists. Your node has the toggle on and no file. The wizard shows that sentence, then asks if the toggle should stay off until you write. You answer. It does not flip the toggle.
2. Help says the file name needs the frame in it, or every frame overwrites one file. Your path has no frame token. The wizard shows the doc’s example path beside an empty field. You type the path. It does not invent `$HIP/geo/hero.$F4.bgeo.sc` for you.
3. You press **Save to Disk** yourself when the answers match the page.

The version line sits at the top of those screens, and only when it is true. Example: this Houdini is 20.5, so the checklist was built from the 20.5 help that shipped with it. The current SideFX website documents 21.0 and describes a parameter this node does not have. That parameter is ignored. You are not following a newer manual onto an older node.

That line is a guardrail. It is not the product. The product is the three questions against the live node.

## What you write

A Python shelf tool, the same kind you have written before. `hou` reads the selected node, its type, the installed version, and the parameter values. A Python panel or a short `hou.ui` sequence shows one step. Nothing else is the interface. There is no chat box.

## Stack, and the part that is easy to overbuild

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  shelf[ShelfOnSelectedNode] --> helpPage[InstalledHelpForThatNode]
  helpPage --> gemma[GemmaBuildsQuestionList]
  gemma --> step[OneQuestionOnScreen]
  step --> you[YouAnswer]
  you --> temporal[TemporalRemembersTheStep]
  temporal --> step
  website[SerpApiChecksWebsiteVersion] --> step
```

- **Skill.** The shape of a step: one doc sentence, the warning before the action, one question, the parameter name that must exist on this node. No suggested artistic value. Gemma’s list is thrown away if it names a parameter the node does not have.
- **Gemma, local.** Turns that node’s installed help into the question list. This is the open-source core. A hand-written checklist for every node would be a different, smaller tool, and it would not need a model.
- **Temporal.** Remembers which step you are on and what you already answered, so a Houdini crash does not restart you at the top. Fetch and extract retry. It is not a second app. Friday time-box: `temporal-agent-harness==0.7.0`, or the Temporal Python SDK if the harness cannot call local Gemma. LangGraph stays out; the harness README still marks that integration as planned.
- **SerpApi.** One lookup: the website page for this node, used only to say whether it documents a different build than the one installed. The questions come from installed help. If that single check is not in the recorded demo, the post does not enter the SerpApi category.

Out: a chat panel, a second harness, hosting, a database, and any button that sets a value you did not type.

# Houdini documentation wizard — Week 3

## The click

You select the node you are working on and click the shelf tool. It reads that node’s installed help and **builds the mechanical setup the page describes**. You answer only the blanks that are your call. Then you go back to the look.

A form that asks you about the page is not this tool. That click adds reading. This click removes the wiring you would otherwise redo from the manual.

Help already opens the right page. The wizard uses the page as a recipe. Each new node gets the one help sentence that justified it, as a comment, so the setup does not become a black box. You can see why the node is there and change it.

Artistic values stay at their defaults, or at the number you typed. The tool does not pick density, color, timing, or scale for beauty. If the help is unclear about whether a parameter is plumbing or a look choice, it asks you. It does not guess.

## Example

You have a mesh and you want points on it. The look you care about is how many points, and whether they relax. The plumbing is the same every time: create a Scatter, wire your mesh into it, set the count mode the help describes, leave the other toggles the way the page says so the count you typed is the count you get.

Before the click: you create the node, wire it, open the help because the count mode is easy to get wrong, fix it, then look at the points.

After the click: you typed the count and yes or no on relax. The Scatter exists, wired, with the help’s count mode already set, and a comment on the node quoting that sentence. You scrub the count and look at the points.

Same shape for a cache, which is pure plumbing. You type a folder. The tool creates a File Cache on the selected node, puts the frame token in the path, and leaves **Load from Disk** off until a file exists. You press **Save to Disk** when you want the write. You skip the hour where every frame overwrote one file.

The version line is one sentence at the top when it matters. The checklist came from the help shipped with this Houdini. The website documents a newer build and mentions a parameter this node does not have, so that parameter was not created.

## What you write

A Python shelf tool. `hou` reads the selection and the installed version, creates the nodes, wires them, and sets only the plumbing parameters. No chat box. No viewport capture.

## Stack

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  shelf[ShelfOnSelectedNode] --> helpPage[InstalledHelp]
  helpPage --> gemma[GemmaSplitsPlumbingFromYourChoices]
  gemma --> ask[YouAnswerOnlyYourChoices]
  ask --> build[ShelfCreatesAndWiresNodes]
  build --> comment[HelpSentenceOnEachNewNode]
  temporal[TemporalRemembersUnfinishedSetup] --> ask
  website[SerpApiWebsiteVsInstall] --> ask
```

# Houdini fast help — Week 3

## The click, in your words

Select a node. Click the shelf tool. The help for that node appears.

It does not ask you anything. It does not build a network. “The look” was a bad phrase for the picture you were making, and it is not part of this tool. After the card is open you keep working on the same node.

Houdini already has this button: the `?` on the node, which calls the help browser. That browser starts a local help server and loads a heavy page. The first open is the slow part artists wait on. Parameter tooltips are instant and only one line. The website is a third copy, often for a newer build than the one installed.

This shelf tool is useful only if it is faster than that `?` button and shows the same installed help. A second slow page does not earn a button. People will use it when the card is up before the official help pane finishes loading.

## How it is fast

The slow work happens once, when you build an index from this Houdini’s help files (`$HFS/houdini/help`), not when you click.

- The index stores one plain-text card per node type.
- The shelf click reads the selected node’s type and opens that card. No help server, no website, no full manual parse on the click.
- The card leads with a short summary (what the node does, the warnings, the parameter names), then the rest of the page text so you can scroll. The summary is why you are not dumped into the raw HTML.

The version problem is handled by the source. The index is built from the help that shipped with the running Houdini, so the card matches the node you clicked. The website is not consulted.

## What each piece does

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  files[InstalledHelpFiles] --> indexBuild[IndexBuiltOnce]
  indexBuild --> cards[PlainTextCards]
  gemma[GemmaWritesSummaryAtTop] --> cards
  click[ShelfClickOnSelectedNode] --> cards
  cards --> panel[CardOpensImmediately]
```

- **Python shelf.** The thing you have written before. `hou` reads the selected node type and opens the card.
- **Gemma, local.** Runs during the index build, not on the click. It writes the summary at the top of each card. A click-time model would make the tool slower, which misses the point. The open-source piece is that summary. The speed is the index.
- **Skill.** Rules for the summary: purpose, warnings, parameter names, no suggested values, no invented parameters. If a summary names a parameter the node does not have, that card is rebuilt or left as the raw text.
- **Temporal.** Only if the index build is long enough that a crash should resume it. It is not on the click path. Friday time-box. If the build is a short Python script, do not wrap it just to enter the category.
- **SerpApi.** Out. A live fetch is slower than the local file, and the website often documents a different build.

Out: questions, node creation, a chat box, a second harness, hosting, a database.

## Why someone uses it over the tools they have

- Official `?` help: right page, slow to open.
- Tooltip: instant, one line, no warnings and no parameter list.
- Website or a forum: leaves Houdini, easy to read the wrong version.
- This shelf: the installed page, summary first, open from the node you already selected, without waiting on the help server.

The before and after to time is that wait. Same node, `?` versus the shelf. Seconds, on a cold help server and on a warm one.

# Houdini section help — Week 3

## The click

Select a node. Click the shelf tool. A card opens.

- **Title:** the parameter you are on, or the node name if no parameter is selected.
- **One line under the title:** what that parameter or node is for. Short. It does not take over the card.
- **Body:** the documentation section for that focus. A parameter section when one is selected. When the node has a cook error, the section that explains that failure. When you only wanted to learn the node, the same card with jumps to each parameter section, so you are not scrolling the full article from the top.

The shelf is an explicit click. It is not a hover tip. Hover tips wait on purpose, many parameters have none, and a tip that appears whenever the cursor pauses is the wrong place for documentation.

## What Houdini already does

The `?` control sits in the node options flag. Parameters do not have that control. They have a hover tip, after a delay, and not on every parameter. The `?` path starts Houdini’s local help server, which turns the installed wiki file into a full HTML article and opens it at the top. That article is a contents list, then every parameter. You scroll, or you follow a link, to the part you needed.

The files are already on disk with the install, under `$HFS/houdini/help`, as wiki text (often inside `nodes.zip`, one file per node type). SideFX also publishes the same docs on the website, one set per release. The `?` page is the installed copy, served locally. It is not a live pull of a newer website. [Central help server](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/help/central.html) describes that server and the static generation path. A 2026 SideFX thread confirms the files live in the install directory, for example `Houdini 21.0.xxx\houdini\help`. [Where can I download/generate the offline docs](https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/103235/).

A cook error on the node is a separate message, like a terminal error plus a hint. It is not the warning paragraph inside the help article. The card does not replace that error. It uses the error text to choose which help section to open.

## What “index” means

An index is a small table of contents for one node’s help file.

Example row: Mountain, Height → the Height section cut out of Mountain’s wiki file, plus a one-line tag.

The first time you open a node type, the shelf reads that one file and cuts it at the parameter headings. It saves the table. The next click opens the row. It does not start the help server, and it does not walk every node in Houdini.

That cut is short because it is one file. A Houdini crash in the middle of a click does not leave a job to resume. You click again. Temporal stays out. There is no long build that needs a harness.

The slowness of `?` is the help server and the full article. This tool avoids both. The model is not what makes the click fast. The click never runs a model.

## Gemma, and what stays out

Gemma runs only while a node’s file is being cut. For each section it writes the one-line tag: when to open this section. Those tags are how a cook error that does not literally name the parameter can still land on the right section. They are stored in the table. The click is a lookup.

SerpApi stays out. The text we want is the file that shipped with this install. A website fetch is slower, and it can be a different release than the node on screen.

Out: hover tips, a chat box, creating nodes, setting values, Temporal, a second harness, hosting, a database.

## Before and after

Same node.

- `?` opens the article at the top. The parameter you wanted is a link further down.
- The shelf card’s title is that parameter, or the cook error’s section, and the body is that part of the local file.

Time the open if it is obvious. The reason to keep the tool is the landing spot, not only the clock.

#  Network editor 

How to create, move, copy, and edit nodes.

##  Viewing¶ 

See navigating networks.

##  Adding nodes¶ 

| To...                                                  | Do this                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create a new node                                      | In the network editor, press ⇥ Tab to open a menu of available node types. Start typing the name of a node and press Enter, or use the menu items to select a node type. Click in the network editor to place the new node. Tip You can drop the node on a [wire](wire.html "How to connect nodes to each other to make them work together.") to automatically insert it between the wire’s input and output.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Create a new node attached to an existing input/output | To branch a new wire off an input or output connector, click the connector to start a wire, then press ⇥ Tab and use the menu to choose which type of node to create and press Enter. To insert a new node just before a connected input, or just after an output, ![](../icons/KEYS/RMB.svg "RMB")\-click the connector and use the menu to choose the type of node to insert. You can press ⇥ Tab, choose the node type, and then while placing the node, you can drag from a connector to wire the node and place it at the same time. You can press ⇥ Tab, choose the node type, and then press ⇧ Shift \+ Enter to automatically wire the new node into the output of the “current” node (the node shown in the parameter editor, usually the most-recently selected node). |
| Create a quick copy of a node                          | Hold Alt and drag the node to drag out a copy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

##  Working with nodes¶ 

| To...                                             | Do this                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Select a node                                     | Click the “body” of the node (not including the [flags](flags.html "Flags represent some state information on the node, such as which node represents the output of the network. Different network types have different flags.")). You can hold S to enter a “select-only” mode. While you hold the key down, clicking and dragging will only select. This makes it easy to select nodes without worrying about moving the node or accidentally clicking wires, flags, or other UI. |

| Delete a node                                     | Select the node and choose **Edit ▸ Delete** or press ⌦ Del. When you delete a node, the network tries to fix itself by connecting all the descendants of the deleted node to the node’s first parent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Move a node                                       | Drag the node. To move the node and all downstream nodes at the same time, hold ⇧ Shift and drag. To move the node and all upstream nodes at the same time, hold ⌃ Ctrl and drag.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

See also [copies and references](copying.html "How to create references between parameters and create node copies that reference the original.").                                                                                                                                                                                  |

##  Node ring¶ 

Hovering over a node pops up a “ring” around the node with access to the node’s flags and a button to open the node info window. This makes it easy to interact with flags when you're zoomed out so far the flag indicators on the node are too tiny to click.

Clicking the flags in the ring is the same as clicking the flag areas on the node. For example, you can use the same keyboard modifiers to separate the display and render flags in a geometry network.

Tip

Hold CTRL to temporarily fade the ring when you want to point to a node the ring is obscuring.

You can turn off the node ring or change the zoom level at which it appears in the network editor options.

##  Node info window¶ 

You can get statistics and information about a particular node in the _info window_. For example, the info window for geometry nodes shows the number of points, primitives, and vertices, as well as the groups and attributes in the node’s geometry. This is often very useful for figuring out what’s going on.

To show the node info window temporarily, hold  on the node. When you release the mouse button, the window automatically closes. To open the node info in a window, hover over the node and click the “i” button in the ring.

See the node info window for more information.

##  Tips¶ 

* You can copy and paste between multiple running instances of Houdini. To make each running copy of Houdini have a separate clipboard, use the `SESI_COPY_SUFFIX` environment variable.

#  Node Info 

The node info window shows a quick overview of statistics and information about a particular node.

| On this page | [How to](#how-to) [Showing SOP attribute changes](#diff) [Controlling info window updates](#updates) [Customizing the info window](#customizing-the-info-window) |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

For example, the info window for geometry nodes shows the number of points, primitives, and vertices, as well as the groups and attributes in the node’s geometry. This is often very useful for figuring out what’s going on.

##  How to¶ 

| To...                                                              | Do this                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Show the info window temporarily to quickly check some information | Hold ![](../icons/KEYS/MMB.svg "MMB") on the node. When you release the mouse button, the window automatically closes. Tip If you hold ⇧ Shift \+ ![](../icons/KEYS/MMB.svg "MMB") the info window opens without cooking the node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Open the info in a window                                          | Hover over the node and click the  button in the ring.  or ⌃ Ctrl \+ ![](../icons/KEYS/MMB.svg "MMB") click the node.  or Right-click the node and choose **Show node information**. As soon as the info window loses focus (for example, you click somewhere outside the window), it closes. This lets you scroll the information and interact with the controls in the window. Tip You can set a preference so an unpinned info window always requires manually closing, instead of disappearing when it loses focus. In the main menus, choose **Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Network editor** and turn off **Node info windows close when losing focus**. Linux On Linux, the default is for the info window to persist even if it loses focus, requiring you to close the window manually. This is because some Linux users turn on a “focus follows mouse” preference, making the info window lose focus immediately and close. If you don’t have “focus follows mouse” on in your window manager, you can turn on the **Node Info Windows Close When Losing Focus** option in **Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Network Editor, Nodes, and Trees**. |
| Keep an info window open persistently                              | Click the ![](../icons/NETVIEW/pin_out.svg) pin icon in the info window. You can click the pin icon again to “unpin” the window.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Pause updates                                                      | By default, while the info window is open it updates to show changes to the node caused by time changes, parameter changes, and input data changes. (Info window updates are limited to roughly 50 times per second in an attempt to avoid affecting Houdini performance.) If you click the pause button in the window window, the information in the window will _not_ automatically update. If something in the node changes, a Refresh button will appear in the window. You can click the Refresh button to update to the current state of the node, or turn off the Pause button to resume automatic updates. See [controlling updates](info.html#updates) below for more information.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Visualize SOP attributes and groups                                | If you open an interactive info window (by ⌃ Ctrl \+ ![](../icons/KEYS/MMB.svg "MMB") clicking a SOP node or clicking the “info” button in a SOP node’s ring), you can click the switch next to the name of an attribute to create and enable a [visualizer](../visualizers/index.html) for that attribute. You can also click the switch next to the name of a group. This will show the group box in the viewer and set it to highlight the group contents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Copy information from the info window                              | If you open an interactive info window (by ⌃ Ctrl \+ ![](../icons/KEYS/MMB.svg "MMB") clicking a SOP node or clicking the “info” button in a SOP node’s halo), you can click tiles to select them, then press ⌃ Ctrl \+ C to copy the tile text. For lists such as the list of attributes of each type, you can also drag-select across items to select them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

##  Showing SOP attribute changes¶ 

The info window for SOP nodes displays lists of attributes in the node’s geometry.

* By default, if a SOP node’s first input is connected, the node’s info window shows attributes added by the node in **bold**. You can turn this off by clicking the gear menu and turning off **Highlight New Attributes**.
* You can switch the attribute list to a “diff” mode that highlights new, deleted, and changed attributes. To switch to diff mode in the info window, turn on the **Show changes to attributes** switch below the attributes, or click the gear menu and turn on **Show changes to attributes** in the menu.  
The show changes mode highlights new attributes in green, deleted attributes in pink, attributes with the same name but different metadata (such as a different default or number of components) in purple, and attributes with changed values in yellow.  
Note  
Diff mode can potentially be slow if the node’s geometry has a large number of attributes or the geometry is very large, for example comparing point attributes on a node with millions of points. This is why showing differences is off by default, and you probably want to turn it off when you're finished using it.

##  Controlling info window updates¶ 

* By default, the info window updates every 0.25 seconds. You can choose a different update frequency in the gear menu.
* To stop automatic updates in the info window, turn on the Pause button, or open the gear menu and set the update frequency to **Manual**.
* While updates are paused, you can manually refresh the window by clicking the Refresh button at the top next to the Pause button.
* Sometimes, for example if a node has an error and then you clear the error, the info window may not automatically reload. You can open the gear menu and choose **Cook and Refresh** to force the node to recook and the info window to refresh the node info.

Note

If the **Edit ▸ Live Parameter Display During Playback** preference is off, the info window does not update during playback either. You can also control this using the **Live Parameter Updates During Playback** parameter in the node info window’s gear menu.

## What Houdini already does

The `?` control sits in the node options flag. Parameters do not have that control. They have a hover tip, after a delay, and not on every parameter. The `?` path starts Houdini’s local help server, which turns the installed wiki file into a full HTML article and opens it at the top. That article is a contents list, then every parameter. You scroll, or you follow a link, to the part you needed.

The files are already on disk with the install, under `$HFS/houdini/help`, as wiki text (often inside `nodes.zip`, one file per node type). SideFX also publishes the same docs on the website, one set per release. The `?` page is the installed copy, served locally. It is not a live pull of a newer website. [Central help server](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/help/central.html) describes that server and the static generation path. A 2026 SideFX thread confirms the files live in the install directory, for example `Houdini 21.0.xxx\houdini\help`. [Where can I download/generate the offline docs](https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/103235/).

A cook error on the node is a separate message, like a terminal error plus a hint. It is not the warning paragraph inside the help article. The card does not replace that error. It uses the error text to choose which help section to open.

Flags are separate from that, and they depend on the network. On a SOP those are bypass, lock (freeze the cooked geometry so upstream does not recook), template, display (the node shown in the viewer), and render. SideFX lists them on the [flags](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/network/flags.html) page, and the ring that holds the **i** is on the [network editor](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/network/nodes.html#info) page. The first time that node type is opened this way, the tool reads Mountain’s help file from the install and cuts out the Height section. Gemma reads that section and writes a short lesson for a beginner: a title, one line on what Height is for, the warning in that section, then the section itself, then one “read next” pointer to another section in the same file (or the input node’s file). It does not tell you a value to type. It does not read every node in Houdini.

The card is that lesson. The `?` page is the whole article from the top. Same sentences. Different order, and only the part that matches the parameter or the cook error.

Temporal runs that as two steps you can leave and come back to: this section, then the one Gemma pointed at. If the Gemma call fails, the step retries. If Houdini quits after the first step, the next click continues on the second section instead of starting over. The harness event stream is the record of those steps. That is the harness job. A crash during a single popup would not have been one.

## What earns a prize, and what overlaps

Aim at Best Use of Gemma. The lesson frame is the model’s work. A chopped paragraph with no lesson is a faster `?`, and that is a weak Gemma entry. Temporal is the second entry because the lesson has steps, retries, and a trace. You can win only one prize. Writing quality still weighs more than the list.

One tool keeps a job when it already covers the next job:

- Temporal’s event stream is the trace, so Sentry stays out.
- Temporal holds which step you are on, so Tiger and Atlas stay out.
- Mastra would be a second harness, so it stays out.
- SerpApi would fetch sidefx.com. That site is another copy of this manual, often another release. The lesson must match the node on screen, so SerpApi stays out.
- Browserbase would open that same website. Out.
- ElevenLabs would read the card aloud. The card is already the reading. Out.
- Render can host a sample card later so a judge without Houdini can open one lesson. It does not make the shelf work. Add it only after the shelf lesson is real.
- TabPFN, Tinker, Arduino, Auth0, Copilot-as-a-product, DigitalOcean, a `.tech` domain, and Ultramarine have no job in this lesson.

A second tool is welcome when its job is different. Gemma writes the lesson. Temporal keeps the steps. Those two do not overlap.

# Stack and flow

Story: [POSITIONING.md](./POSITIONING.md). This diagram is the one to embed in the DEV post. Update it here if the click changes.

## Stack

| Piece | Choice | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shelf | Python in Houdini (`hou`) | Read the selected node, the selected parameter, and any cook error. Show the card. |
| Manual | The help file in this install (`$HFS/houdini/help`) | The words on the card. Quoted. |
| Model | Gemma, local, through Ollama | Pick the heading. Do not write a new sentence or a parameter value. |
| Skill | `skills/houdini-section/SKILL.md` | Quote the section. If no heading matches, list the headings. |
| Resume | Temporal Python SDK (`temporalio`) | One workflow: retry the pick, and return this same card if Houdini quits while the user is still on the node. |
| Code history | Entire | `entire search` over past agent work to explain why shelf code exists. Not shown on the node. |

The experimental Temporal agent harness (four local processes) is not the stack. This click is one card. The Python SDK is the Temporal entry. Sentry stays out because the workflow history is the trace.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  user[UserOnANode] --> shelf[ShelfClick]
  shelf --> localFile[InstalledHelpFile]
  localFile --> gemma[GemmaPicksOneHeading]
  gemma --> quote[CardQuotesThatSection]
  gemma --> listHeads[NoMatchListsHeadings]
  quote --> temporal[TemporalKeepsThisCard]
  listHeads --> temporal
  temporal --> back[UserChangesTheNode]
```

1. You select a node. You may also have a parameter selected, or the node may show a cook error.
2. The shelf click reads that from Houdini. It does not open the `?` page and it does not start the help server.
3. It opens the one wiki file for that node type from the install.
4. Gemma chooses one heading. A selected parameter wins. Otherwise it matches the cook error to the headings in that file.
5. The card title is that heading. The body is the section, copied from the file. If nothing matches, the card says so and lists the headings. No guessed paragraph. No value to type.
6. Temporal keeps that card. A failed model call retries. If Houdini quits, the next click brings the same card back. A new cook error starts a card for the new error.
7. You change the node yourself.

Entire sits beside this, on the repo. After sessions exist, `entire search` is how we show why a function was written. It is not a step in the shelf click.

# Entire

Entire explains why shelf code exists by searching past agent work. It is not the card on the node. Docs: [https://docs.entire.io/overview](https://docs.entire.io/overview).

The dashboard stays empty until this folder is a git repo, Entire is enabled, a commit exists, and the repo is on your Entire account. This file is the setup. Do not import old Cursor history from other projects.

## One-time setup

From `d:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard`:

```bash
entire login
entire enable --agent cursor --init-repo --yes --search-skill --initial-commit-message "Start the Houdini section card notes for Week 3."
entire status
entire session current
```

`entire enable --init-repo` creates the git repo if needed and the first commit. It does not create a remote and it does not push. `--yes` does not import the last 30 days of agent history.

If the repo already exists, skip `--init-repo`:

```bash
entire enable --agent cursor --yes --search-skill
```

## Add the repo on the dashboard

After `entire login`, add this repository in the Entire dashboard, or create it from the CLI once you know the project name:

```bash
entire project list
entire repo create houdini-wizard --project <project-name>
```

Do not run `repo create` twice if the first one succeeded and only the readiness check failed.

Checkpoints show up on the dashboard after a commit is pushed to the remote Entire is syncing. `entire status` names that remote. Until you add the remote, sessions stay on this machine.

## Later, when a commit has no session

```bash
entire session list
entire session attach <cursor-session-id> --agent cursor
entire search "why the shelf quotes the heading"
entire checkpoint explain <id>
```

The Cursor session id is the transcript filename without `.jsonl`, or whatever `entire session current` prints.

`entire search` is the demo for the post: a query about why a piece of the shelf exists, then `checkpoint explain` on one hit. Run that after there is real shelf code and at least one checkpoint, not on this notes-only commit.

# Build the shelf card

The public flow stays [FLOW.md](d:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard\FLOW.md). Personal notes stay in `hacktoberfest-week3/` and stay gitignored. New code is what gets committed.

## Language and resources

- **Python**, the same interpreter Houdini ships (`hython`). The shelf is a thin `hou` script. The quote, heading list, and model call are plain modules so they can run without a Houdini UI.
- **Installed help** under `$HFS/houdini/help` (wiki text, often `nodes.zip/<category>/<name>.txt`). A small fixture file in the repo stands in for that path during tests.
- **Gemma through Ollama** on localhost. The model receives only the list of headings and the cook error. It must return one heading from that list, or none. It never writes the card body and never names a parameter value.
- **Temporal Python SDK** (`temporalio`), one workflow. Not the four-process agent harness. A local `temporal server start-dev` plus one worker. The workflow retries the heading pick and remembers the card (node path, heading, quoted section) so the next shelf click after a quit shows the same card. A new cook error is a new card.
- **Skill** at `skills/houdini-section/SKILL.md`: quote the file, pick only from the given headings, say none when nothing matches.
- **Entire** stays off this click. No SerpApi, no second harness, no hosted runtime.

## Click logic

1. Selected parameter whose name matches a heading: quote that section. Gemma is not called.
2. Cook error whose text contains a heading: quote that section. Gemma is not called.
3. Cook error that does not name a heading: Gemma picks one heading from the list, or none. Temporal runs this call.
4. No match: the card lists the file’s headings. The user opens one. The shelf does not choose the next topic.

The card title is the heading. The body is the section copied from the file.

## Files

- `skills/houdini-section/SKILL.md`
- `src/houdini_wizard/help_file.py` — open one node file, split on headings
- `src/houdini_wizard/card.py` — quote or heading list
- `src/houdini_wizard/pick.py` — exact match, then Ollama constrained to the heading list
- `src/houdini_wizard/workflow.py` — Temporal workflow and worker
- `src/houdini_wizard/shelf.py` — `hou` selection, dialog, start-or-restore workflow
- `fixtures/` — one sample node help file and one cook-error string that does not equal a heading
- `pyproject.toml` — `temporalio` and a stdlib HTTP call to Ollama. No web-search client.
- [README.md](d:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard\README.md) — how to run the worker, pull the local Gemma tag, and install the shelf. The diagram in `FLOW.md` stays the one for the DEV post.

## Check

A fixture run prints the quoted section for a known heading, the heading list when Gemma would return none, and a restored card from the same workflow id. The Houdini dialog is the same text. The user still changes the node.

Development style for this challenge: local model (Gemma over Ollama) + one skill + local files (the Houdini help tree) + the Houdini Python API (`hou` in hython) + the Temporal Python SDK. The model only returns a heading. Python quotes the matching section from the file. Many clicks never call the model, because a selected parameter or a cook error already names a heading.

This is not an agent loop, and the shelf does not speak MCP. We do not train or fine-tune Gemma. Entire records the build for later review and is outside this runtime.

- **Skill, one file.** `skills/houdini-section/SKILL.md` is the instruction sent with the heading-pick call. It tells Gemma to return one heading from the list it was given, or none, and it forbids a new sentence and a parameter value. That file is the addition. A normal Ollama chat does not behave this way.
- **No master prompt.** Python decides the four click cases. There is no second prompt that manages skills, tools, or a loop. The skill is used only when the cook error does not already name a heading.
- **Temporal Python SDK** (`temporalio`). One workflow retries that pick and stores the card. The shelf, running in hython, reads the selected node and the one help member. The worker does not need a Houdini install. The experimental agent harness (Code Mode, callback tools, browser UI, session-manager) stays unused. The durable part we want is this workflow.
- **hython.** The `hou` module reads the selection and opens the dialog. The quote, heading list, and model call are plain modules so a fixture can run without the Houdini UI.
- **Entire, off the click.** Cursor hooks and `entire search` / `entire checkpoint explain` map why the shelf code exists. The running card does not call Entire.
- **No MCP.** The shelf talks to Ollama over localhost HTTP and to Temporal over its Python SDK. MCP is not a dependency of this tool.

---
name: houdini-section
description: Sent to Gemma only when a cook error does not already name a heading. This file is an addition to the model. A normal Ollama chat does not follow it.
---

You choose one heading from a Houdini help file.

The user message lists the headings and one cook error. Reply with JSON only. The JSON has one field, `heading`.

- `heading` is copied from that list, character for character, or the exact word `none`.
- Do not write a sentence.
- Do not explain the node.
- Do not name a parameter value.
- If none of the headings is about that error, `heading` is `none`.

"""One Temporal Python workflow. It retries the heading pick and restores the card."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import hashlib
from datetime import timedelta

from temporalio import activity, workflow
from temporalio.client import Client
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy, WorkflowIDReusePolicy
from temporalio.exceptions import WorkflowAlreadyStartedError
from temporalio.worker import Worker

TASK_QUEUE = "houdini-wizard"

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from houdini_wizard.card import card_from_heading
    from houdini_wizard.pick import pick_heading


@activity.defn(name="pick_heading_activity")
async def pick_heading_activity(request: dict) -> str:
    return pick_heading(request["headings"], request["error_text"])


@workflow.defn
class CardWorkflow:
    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        heading = request.get("known_heading") or ""
        if not heading and request.get("needs_model"):
            heading = await workflow.execute_activity(
                pick_heading_activity,
                {"headings": request.get("headings") or [], "error_text": request.get("error_text") or ""},
                start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=90),
                retry_policy=RetryPolicy(maximum_attempts=3),
            )
        return card_from_heading(request.get("sections") or [], heading or None)


def workflow_id(node_path: str, parm_name: str, error_text: str) -> str:
    raw = f"{node_path}\n{parm_name}\n{error_text.strip()}"
    return "wizard-" + hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32]


async def open_card(client: Client, card_id: str, request: dict) -> dict:
    try:
        return await client.execute_workflow(
            CardWorkflow.run,
            request,
            id=card_id,
            task_queue=TASK_QUEUE,
            id_reuse_policy=WorkflowIDReusePolicy.REJECT_DUPLICATE,
        )
    except WorkflowAlreadyStartedError:
        handle = client.get_workflow_handle(card_id)
        return await handle.result()


async def connect(address: str | None = None) -> Client:
    import os

    target = address or os.environ.get("TEMPORAL_ADDRESS", "localhost:7233")
    return await Client.connect(target)


async def run_worker() -> None:
    client = await connect()
    worker = Worker(
        client,
        task_queue=TASK_QUEUE,
        workflows=[CardWorkflow],
        activities=[pick_heading_activity],
    )
    print(f"Houdini wizard worker on {TASK_QUEUE}")
    await worker.run()


def main() -> None:
    asyncio.run(run_worker())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Check the quote, the heading list, and a card restored by the same workflow id."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from temporalio.testing import WorkflowEnvironment
from temporalio.worker import Worker

from houdini_wizard.help_file import load_path, load_zip_member
from houdini_wizard.pick import decide
from houdini_wizard.workflow import TASK_QUEUE, CardWorkflow, open_card, pick_heading_activity, workflow_id

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE = ROOT / "fixtures" / "box.txt"
UNNAMED = "Primitive count exceeds the point limit for this cook."
INSTALL_ZIP = Path(r"C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 22.0.466\houdini\help\nodes.zip")


def fail(message: str) -> None:
    print(f"FAIL {message}")
    sys.exit(1)


def check_file(path: Path) -> None:
    loaded = load_path(str(path))
    headings = [section.heading for section in loaded.sections]
    if "Polygon" in headings:
        fail("a menu choice was treated as a heading")
    size = next(section for section in loaded.sections if section.heading == "Size")
    if "sizex" not in [channel.lstrip("/") for channel in size.channels]:
        fail("Size is missing the sizex channel")
    if "Size of the box along xyz axes." not in size.body:
        fail("Size quote is missing the installed sentence")

    quoted = decide(loaded.sections, "sizex", "Size", "")
    if quoted["needs_model"] or quoted["known_heading"] != "Size":
        fail(f"selected Size still called Gemma: {quoted['known_heading']!r}")
    print("Quote: Size")
    print(size.body)
    print()

    named = decide(loaded.sections, "", "", "Uniform Scale must be greater than zero.")
    if named["needs_model"] or named["known_heading"] != "Uniform Scale":
        fail("cook error that names Uniform Scale did not quote it")
    print("Quote from cook error: Uniform Scale")
    print()

    unnamed = decide(loaded.sections, "", "", UNNAMED)
    if not unnamed["needs_model"] or unnamed["known_heading"]:
        fail("an unnamed cook error skipped Gemma")
    print("No heading named. The file's headings:")
    for heading in unnamed["headings"]:
        print(f"- {heading}")
    print()


def check_install() -> None:
    if not INSTALL_ZIP.is_file():
        print("Installed nodes.zip was not on this machine. Fixture file only.")
        print()
        return
    loaded = load_zip_member(str(INSTALL_ZIP), "sop/box.txt")
    headings = [section.heading for section in loaded.sections]
    if "Size" not in headings or "Polygon" in headings:
        fail(f"installed sop/box.txt headings look wrong: {headings[:12]}")
    size = next(section for section in loaded.sections if section.heading == "Size")
    if "Size of the box along xyz axes." not in size.body:
        fail("installed Size section was not quoted")
    print(f"Installed help: {loaded.source}")
    print(f"Headings: {len(headings)}. Menu choice Polygon stayed inside Primitive Type.")
    print()


async def check_restore() -> None:
    import houdini_wizard.pick as pick_mod

    loaded = load_path(str(FIXTURE))
    calls = {"n": 0}
    original = pick_mod.pick_heading

    def fake(headings: list[str], error_text: str) -> str:
        calls["n"] += 1
        return "none"

    pick_mod.pick_heading = fake
    try:
        async with await WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping() as env:
            worker = Worker(
                env.client,
                task_queue=TASK_QUEUE,
                workflows=[CardWorkflow],
                activities=[pick_heading_activity],
            )
            async with worker:
                quoted = decide(loaded.sections, "scale", "Uniform Scale", "")
                card_id = workflow_id("/obj/geo1/box1", "scale", "")
                first = await open_card(env.client, card_id, quoted)
                second = await open_card(env.client, card_id, quoted)
                if first["title"] != "Uniform Scale" or second["title"] != first["title"]:
                    fail("the same workflow id did not restore the quote")
                if calls["n"] != 0:
                    fail("Gemma ran for a heading that was already named")
                print(f"Restored card: {second['title']}")

                unnamed = decide(loaded.sections, "", "", UNNAMED)
                other_id = workflow_id("/obj/geo1/box1", "", UNNAMED)
                listed = await open_card(env.client, other_id, unnamed)
                again = await open_card(env.client, other_id, unnamed)
                if listed["kind"] != "list" or again["headings"] != listed["headings"]:
                    fail("the unnamed error did not restore the heading list")
                if calls["n"] != 1:
                    fail(f"Gemma ran {calls['n']} times for one card")
                print("Restored heading list from the same workflow id. Gemma ran once.")
    finally:
        pick_mod.pick_heading = original


def main() -> None:
    os.chdir(ROOT)
    check_file(FIXTURE)

# Houdini wizard tool

Shelf tool for Houdini. You select a node, or a parameter whose channel is selected, or you are stuck on a cook error. The card quotes the matching section from the help that shipped with this install.

![Flow](docs/flow.svg)

The same labels are in [FLOW.md](FLOW.md).

You still change the node. The shelf does not set a value.

## What is added to Gemma

Gemma does not know this shelf. `skills/houdini-section/SKILL.md` is sent only when a cook error does not already name a heading. It tells the model to return one heading from the list it was given, or `none`. A normal Ollama chat can paraphrase the help or invent a number. This file forbids both.

Python quotes the section. The model never writes the card.

Add another file under `skills/` when a later call needs its own constraint, and name it here.

## Help files

Houdini stores node help as wiki text in `$HFS/houdini/help/nodes.zip`. One member is one node, for example `sop/box.txt`.

A heading is a `= Title =` line, a `== Folder ==` line, or a parameter `Label:` under `@parameters`. The real parameter names are on the next `#channels:` line (`/sizex` belongs to Size). A more-indented `Label:` is a menu choice and stays inside that parameter's quote.

The shelf opens that one member. It does not extract the zip, scan other nodes, or start the help server behind `?`. The split for that member is kept for the rest of the Houdini session.

## Model

This click is one constrained choice, so the model to pull is `gemma3:4b`. It is the speed and accuracy balance for a short JSON heading. Ollama's `format` schema limits the reply to a heading from the file, or `none`.

`deepseek-r1:8b` is a reasoning model. It spends the click on a hidden chain of thought. Leave it for other work.

```powershell
ollama pull gemma3:4b
```

To use another Gemma tag, set `HOUDINI_WIZARD_MODEL` before the worker starts.

## Temporal

One Python workflow retries the heading pick and restores this card. A new cook error is a new card. This is the Temporal Python SDK, not the multi-process agent harness.

The Temporal CLI is separate from the Python package. Install it, then start the dev server:

```powershell
winget install --id Temporal.TemporalCLI -e
temporal server start-dev
```

CLI docs: https://docs.temporal.io/cli

In a second terminal, from this repo:

```powershell
py -3 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e .
.venv\Scripts\python -m houdini_wizard.fixture
.venv\Scripts\python -m houdini_wizard.workflow
```

The fixture quotes Size, lists headings for an error that names none, and restores both cards from the same workflow id. The worker prints `Houdini wizard worker on houdini-wizard` and stays running.

## Install the shelf in Houdini 22

This machine's hython is Python 3.13, same as the worker. Install the package into hython so the shelf can import it:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 22.0.466\bin\hython.exe" -m pip install --user -e "D:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard"
```

Use the `hython.exe` next to the Houdini you actually open.

Copy `shelf/houdini_wizard.shelf` into the toolbar folder for that version:

`Documents\houdini22.0\toolbar\houdini_wizard.shelf`

Restart Houdini. The shelf tab is **Houdini Wizard**. The tool is **Section card**.

1. Select a node.
2. To quote one parameter, click its name so that channel is selected, then click the shelf. The label or the `#channels` name has to match a heading. Gemma is not called.
3. A cook error that already contains a heading quotes that section. Gemma is not called.
4. A cook error that does not name a heading asks Gemma, inside the Temporal workflow.
5. If nothing matches, the dialog lists the file's headings. You open one.

Ollama, `temporal server start-dev`, and the worker need to be running for the Gemma pick and for restore after a quit. If Temporal is down, the shelf still shows the quote and says the card was not stored.

Entire records this build so a later search can explain why the shelf skips Gemma. The click does not call Entire.
