## Temporal

The feature is one durable Workflow, written with the Temporal Python SDK. It is not the multi-process agent harness, and the CLI is not the feature. The CLI only runs a local Temporal Service so that workflow has somewhere to live.

`CardWorkflow` does two things:

- The heading pick is an Activity with three attempts. If Gemma fails, Temporal runs that call again. A heading that was already named never becomes an Activity.
- The card's id is a Workflow id. The same node and the same cook error reuse that id (`REJECT_DUPLICATE`). The next shelf click returns the stored result and does not call Gemma again. A new cook error is a new id, and a new card.

Open [http://localhost:8233](http://localhost:8233) while the dev server is running. That Web UI is the history of the card: the Workflow, the Activity, and the result. That page is the thing to show in the write-up.

### Where the CLI installs

`winget install --id Temporal.TemporalCLI -e` installs version 1.9.1 as a portable zip, not an MSI and not into Houdini or this repo. WinGet unpacks `temporal.exe` under your user profile (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\`) and puts a `temporal` command on your PATH. It does not change Houdini. Open a new PowerShell window after the install so the command is visible. Confirm with `where.exe temporal`.

Docs: [Run a development server](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/run-a-development-server).

Start it and leave that window open:

```powershell
temporal server start-dev --db-filename D:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard\.temporal\dev.db
```

That process is the whole local service: `localhost:7233` for the SDK, and the Web UI at `http://localhost:8233`. The `--db-filename` flag stores the card in SQLite, so quitting Houdini does not drop it. Without that flag the server keeps the history in memory only, and stopping the server erases the cards. Ctrl+C stops the server.

### The worker

The worker is our Python process, already installed in `.venv`. It is not part of the CLI. It connects to `localhost:7233` and waits on the task queue `houdini-wizard`. The shelf starts the Workflow. The worker runs it, including the Gemma Activity.

In a second terminal:

```powershell
D:\Documents\vscode\houdini-wizard\.venv\Scripts\python -m houdini_wizard.workflow
```

It prints `Houdini wizard worker on houdini-wizard` and stays running. The shelf can show a quote with both of these stopped. Restore, and a Gemma pick, need the server and the worker.

What runs is one worker on the PC, three inboxes (UI, API, Review), SQLite on the PC, and a phone page. One task runs at a time, which matches a 6 GB GPU. The phone reaches the laptop that is running this app through that laptop's Tailscale address, on port 3000. The hub stays on `127.0.0.1:8797` and is not opened to the network. Port 8787 is left for other local apps. Do not port-forward either port.

## Run this on your own laptop

GitHub has the source. It does not have the programs or the secrets this laptop grew while the project was being built. Each person installs those once, on their machine. `pip` and `npm` then download the libraries. Nothing in that download is copied from the author's `.venv`.

### What a clone does not include

These are on the author's machine and are listed in `.gitignore`. A new user needs their own copies. They never receive the author's keys, database, or installed binaries.

| Left on the author's machine | What the new user does |
| --- | --- |
| `.venv/` (Python 3.12 and the packages pip installed, including Aider) | Install Python 3.12, create a new `.venv`, run `pip install` |
| `apps/console/node_modules/` | Install Node.js, then run `npm install` |
| `.env` (API keys, console PIN, folder paths) | Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in their own values |
| `*.db` (the task queue) | Created on their laptop the first time the hub starts |
| `.aider*` (Aider's chat log and repo-map cache) | Aider creates these locally if they use it |
| Ollama models such as `gemma3:4b` | Only if they choose a local model: install Ollama and `ollama pull` |

### Programs to install once

Install these before the project commands. The project does not install them for you.

1. **Git.** Aider uses it to edit a repo. On Windows, install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win). Check with `git --version`.
2. **Python 3.12**, not 3.14 and not only 3.13. Aider does not install on 3.13, which is why this project uses a 3.12 virtual environment. On Windows, install from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31210/) and turn on "Add python.exe to PATH", or run `winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 -e`. Check with `py -3.12 --version`. You should see `Python 3.12` and a version number.
3. **Node.js 20 LTS** or newer. The phone page is a Next.js app. Install from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/) or `winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e`. Check with `node -v` and `npm -v`.
4. **Tailscale on this laptop and on the phone**, signed into the same Tailscale account. That account is theirs. Install from [tailscale.com](https://tailscale.com/download). This is the private path from their phone browser to their laptop. It is not a connection to anyone else's running copy.
5. **Ollama, only for a local model.** Skip this if they will use their own Gemini key. Install from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/download). The pull happens in the steps below.

### Clone, then make a private `.env`

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/<your-name>/agent-team.git
cd agent-team
copy .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` in an editor. Set these to their own values:

- `CONSOLE_PIN` is the password they will type on the phone. Replace `change-me`.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` is a key from their own [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey) account, if `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=gemini`.
- For a local model instead, set `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=ollama` and leave the Gemini key unused.
- `HACKSWARM_REPO_ROOTS` is a folder on their disk that the worker is allowed to edit, for example `C:\Users\TheirName\Projects`. The example path `D:\Documents\vscode` is only this machine's folder.
- Leave `CENTRAL_HUB_URL` alone for the phone console. The phone talks to port 3000 on this laptop. The page then calls the hub at `127.0.0.1:8797` on the same laptop. Do not put someone else's Tailscale address here.

`.env` is gitignored. Their keys stay on their computer as long as they do not force-add that file.

### Python packages download on their own

`pip install` is the trigger. With Python 3.12 installed, these commands create an empty `.venv` and download `aider-chat==0.86.2` and the hub packages from PyPI into it. The first run can take several minutes. A folder of about 600 MB appears and stays untracked.

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

If `py -3.12` is not recognized, Python 3.12 is not installed yet. Install it from the list above and open a new PowerShell window. Do not copy a `.venv` folder from another computer. Those binaries only match the machine that created them.

On macOS or Linux the same two steps are `python3.12 -m venv .venv` and `.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`.

### The phone page downloads on its own

`npm install` reads `apps/console/package.json` and downloads Next.js from the npm registry into `node_modules`. That folder is gitignored too.

```powershell
cd apps\console
npm install
cd ..\..
```

### Start the two processes

Leave both windows open. The worker starts inside the hub because `.env` sets `HACKSWARM_WORKER=1`.

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python -m uvicorn central_hub.api.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8797
```

```powershell
cd apps\console
npm run dev
```

The hub listens only on this laptop. The phone page listens on port 3000 for this laptop's network interfaces, which is how Tailscale can reach it. Do not port-forward 3000 or 8797 on a router.

### Open it on the desktop and on the phone

On the laptop, open `http://127.0.0.1:3000` and sign in with the `CONSOLE_PIN` from their `.env`.

On the phone, Tailscale has to be connected to the same account as the laptop. In PowerShell on the laptop:

```powershell
tailscale ip -4
```

On the phone's browser, open `http://<that-address>:3000`. Example: if the command prints `100.64.12.34`, the phone opens `http://100.64.12.34:3000`. That address is this laptop, not the author's. Sign in with the same PIN.

In Access, set a project folder on their disk. Optional standing rules go in `HACKSWARM.md` inside that project. Then send a task from the Board. The lamp on the card and the Log show the worker on their laptop.

If they chose Ollama, install it, run `ollama pull gemma3:4b`, set `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=ollama` in `.env`, and start the hub again. `deepseek-r1:8b` is optional and slow. Leave it unused unless they already pulled it for something else.

Updates they pull with `git pull` show up on their desktop and their phone after they restart the two processes. A pull does not replace `.env` or `.venv`.

input.contents:
# HackSwarm agent team

Run this on your own laptop. Open it in a browser on that laptop and on your phone. Tailscale connects your phone to your laptop. It does not connect you to anyone else's computer. Your API keys stay in a local `.env` file. Your Python install stays in a local `.venv` folder. Git does not upload either one.

Follow the steps in order. Each step is required unless it says optional.

## 1. Install the programs

The repository does not contain these. Install them on the laptop before cloning.

1. [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win). Aider uses Git to edit a project. Check with `git --version`.
2. [Python 3.12 for Windows](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/). Aider does not install on Python 3.13, so this project uses a 3.12 virtual environment. Turn on "Add python.exe to PATH" in the installer, or run `winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 -e`. Open a new PowerShell window and check with `py -3.12 --version`. The reply must start with `Python 3.12`.
3. [Node.js 20 LTS](https://nodejs.org/) or newer. The phone page is a Next.js app. Or run `winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e`. Check with `node -v` and `npm -v`.
4. [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download) on the laptop and on the phone, both signed into your Tailscale account. That is the private path from the phone browser to this laptop.

Ollama is optional. Skip it if you will use a Gemini key. For a model that stays on the laptop, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) now. The model download is in step 4.

## 2. Clone the repository

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/AbisoyeOnanuga/agent-team.git
cd agent-team
```

## 3. Create your private `.env`

```powershell
copy .env.example .env
```

Open `.env` in an editor and set your own values:

- `CONSOLE_PIN` is the password you will type on the phone. Replace `change-me`.
- For Gemini, create a key in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey), put it in `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and leave `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=gemini`.
- For a local model, set `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=ollama` and leave the Gemini key unused.
- `HACKSWARM_REPO_ROOTS` is a folder on your disk that the worker may edit, for example `C:\Users\YourName\Projects`. `D:\Documents\vscode` in the example is only one machine's path.

Leave `HACKSWARM_WORKER=1`. The hub starts the worker when that is set. `.env` is listed in `.gitignore`. Do not force-add it.

## 4. Create the virtual environment

This step is required. The author uses a `.venv` on their laptop, and you need your own. Git does not include it. `pip` downloads the packages from PyPI onto your machine. The first run can take several minutes and creates a folder of about 600 MB.

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

`requirements.txt` includes `aider-chat==0.86.2` and the hub packages. If `py -3.12` is not recognized, go back to step 1 and open a new PowerShell window after Python 3.12 is installed. Do not copy a `.venv` folder from another computer.

On macOS or Linux, use `python3.12 -m venv .venv` and `.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`.

If you chose Ollama in step 3, pull the model now, from [Ollama's library](https://ollama.com/library/gemma3):

```powershell
ollama pull gemma3:4b
```

## 5. Install the phone page

`npm install` downloads Next.js into `apps/console/node_modules`. That folder is gitignored too.

```powershell
cd apps\console
npm install
cd ..\..
```

## 6. Start the hub

Leave this window open. The worker starts inside this process.

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python -m uvicorn central_hub.api.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8797
```

The hub listens only on the laptop, at `http://127.0.0.1:8797`. Do not port-forward this port.

## 7. Start the phone page

Open a second PowerShell window in the same `agent-team` folder. Leave it open.

```powershell
cd apps\console
npm run dev
```

This listens on port 3000. Do not port-forward that port on your router. Tailscale is how the phone reaches it.

## 8. Open it on the laptop

In a browser on the laptop, open [http://127.0.0.1:3000](http://127.0.0.1:3000). Sign in with the `CONSOLE_PIN` from your `.env`. Eight wrong attempts lock the console for 15 minutes.

## 9. Open it on your phone

Tailscale must be connected on the phone and on the laptop, on your account. On the laptop:

```powershell
tailscale ip -4
```

On the phone's browser, open `http://<that-address>:3000`. If the command prints `100.64.12.34`, the phone opens `http://100.64.12.34:3000`. That address is your laptop. Sign in with the same PIN.

## 10. Point each role at a project

The bottom bar is Board, Log, Approve, Notes, and Access.

1. Open Access.
2. Choose Gemini or the local Ollama model. Gemini needs the key from step 3. Ollama needs `gemma3:4b` from step 4.
3. Set a project folder for each role. The same folder can be used for all three. Save folders.
4. Routine mode waits before a commit, a delete, or an install. Open mode lets a commit land without waiting. Push never runs from the phone.

## 11. Send a task

1. Open Board.
2. Fill in Title and What should change.
3. Choose the agent (UI, API, or Review). These are three queues, not three models. They share the model you picked in Access.
4. Press Queue it.
5. One task runs at a time. The next role waits until the current task is closed.
6. The card lamp shows Idle, Editing, Waiting, or Dry-run. Dry-run means no model is configured. Add the Gemini key or switch to Ollama.
7. Open Log to watch the work. Open Approve when a lamp says Waiting.

A task sent from the phone writes `.hackswarm/notes.md` in the project folder you saved. Put the change you want in What should change. Optional standing rules go in `HACKSWARM.md` in that project. The worker reads the first 4000 characters of that file on every task.

## What the clone does not include

| On the author's machine only | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| `.venv/` | Step 4 |
| `apps/console/node_modules/` | Step 5 |
| `.env` | Step 3 |
| `*.db` task queue | Created the first time the hub starts |
| `.aider*` chat log and repo-map cache | Aider creates these locally when it edits |
| Ollama models | Step 4, only if you chose Ollama |

`git pull` updates the source on your laptop. Restart the two windows from steps 6 and 7 to see it on the desktop and the phone. A pull does not replace your `.env` or your `.venv`.

The picture in `central_hub/dashboard/visualizer.html` is a desk simulation. It is not the live console.

## Models you can switch on

- No key: the queues, the log, and approval still work. Edits stay a dry-run.
- Gemini: `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=gemini` and your `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The editor model is `gemini-3.8-flash`.
- Ollama on this laptop: `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=ollama` and `gemma3:4b`. Slower than Gemini. Expect tens of seconds for an edit.
- xAI, only if you want Grok outside Cursor: a key from [console.x.ai](https://console.x.ai/), `XAI_API_KEY`, and `HACKSWARM_PROVIDER=grok`. Cursor's Grok subscription is not a key for this app.

Mistral, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, OpenCode, Copilot, and Groq are not part of this phone console.

## Earlier notes

The sections above this heading are the original fork: a shared hub, OpenHands, OpenCode, and several free API accounts. This phone console does not start them. Use steps 1 through 11 to run your own copy.

"""A help panel for the node that is open, not a script message box."""

from __future__ import annotations

from houdini_wizard.context import build_study
from houdini_wizard.help_file import Section


def show_panel(sections: tuple[Section, ...] | list[Section], scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str = "") -> None:
    try:
        _qt_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note)
    except Exception:
        _plain_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note)


def _qt_panel(sections, scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str) -> None:
    try:
        from PySide6 import QtCore, QtWidgets
    except ImportError:
        from PySide2 import QtCore, QtWidgets
    import hou

    study = build_study(sections, scene, focus_heading)
    if extra_note:
        study["note"] = f"{extra_note}\n\n{study['note']}".strip()

    dialog = QtWidgets.QDialog(hou.qt.mainWindow())
    dialog.setWindowFlags(QtCore.Qt.Window)
    dialog.setWindowTitle(study["type_label"])
    dialog.resize(760, 680)
    dialog.setStyleSheet(_STYLE)

    root = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout(dialog)
    root.setContentsMargins(28, 24, 28, 20)
    root.setSpacing(12)

    where = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["where"])
    where.setObjectName("where")
    where.setWordWrap(True)
    root.addWidget(where)

    title = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["type_label"])
    title.setObjectName("title")
    root.addWidget(title)

    path = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["path"])
    path.setObjectName("path")
    root.addWidget(path)

    if study["error"]:
        error = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["error"])
        error.setObjectName("error")
        error.setWordWrap(True)
        root.addWidget(error)

    note = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["note"])
    note.setObjectName("note")
    note.setWordWrap(True)
    root.addWidget(note)

    columns = QtWidgets.QHBoxLayout()
    columns.addWidget(_group(QtWidgets, "Wired in", study["wires_in"] or ["This node has no inputs."]))
    columns.addWidget(_group(QtWidgets, "Wired onward", study["wires_out"] or ["This node has no outputs."]))
    root.addLayout(columns)

    if study["folders"]:
        tabs = QtWidgets.QLabel("Parameter window: " + "  ·  ".join(study["folders"]))
        tabs.setObjectName("tabs")
        tabs.setWordWrap(True)
        root.addWidget(tabs)

    if study["related"]:
        related = QtWidgets.QLabel("Often used with: " + ", ".join(study["related"]))
        related.setObjectName("related")
        related.setWordWrap(True)
        root.addWidget(related)

    quote_title = QtWidgets.QLabel(study["focus_heading"] or "Help")
    quote_title.setObjectName("quoteTitle")
    root.addWidget(quote_title)

    quote = QtWidgets.QTextEdit()
    quote.setReadOnly(True)
    quote.setPlainText(study["focus_body"] or "This heading has no text in the installed file.")
    root.addWidget(quote, 1)

    picker = QtWidgets.QComboBox()
    picker.addItems(study["headings"])
    if study["focus_heading"] in study["headings"]:
        picker.setCurrentText(study["focus_heading"])

    def swap() -> None:
        chosen = picker.currentText()
        next_study = build_study(sections, scene, chosen)
        quote_title.setText(next_study["focus_heading"])
        quote.setPlainText(next_study["focus_body"] or "This heading has no text in the installed file.")
        note.setText(next_study["note"])

    picker.currentTextChanged.connect(swap)
    root.addWidget(picker)

    close = QtWidgets.QPushButton("Back to the node")
    close.clicked.connect(dialog.accept)
    root.addWidget(close)
    dialog.exec()


def _group(qt, title: str, lines: list[str]):
    box = qt.QGroupBox(title)
    layout = qt.QVBoxLayout(box)
    label = qt.QLabel("\n\n".join(lines))
    label.setWordWrap(True)
    layout.addWidget(label)
    return box


def _plain_panel(sections, scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str) -> None:
    import hou

    study = build_study(sections, scene, focus_heading)
    text = "\n\n".join(
        part
        for part in (
            study["where"],
            study["error"],
            extra_note,
            study["note"],
            "\n".join(study["wires_in"]),
            study["focus_body"],
        )
        if part
    )
    hou.ui.displayMessage(text, title=study["type_label"])


_STYLE = """
QDialog { background: #241f1b; color: #f4efe6; }
QLabel { color: #f4efe6; font-size: 14px; }
QLabel#where { color: #d7a15a; font-size: 13px; }

The shelf was repeating the help page in a plain message box. It now opens a panel for the node you have selected, and the help text stays a quote from the file that shipped with this Houdini.

The panel adds what that page does not know about your scene:

- Which network you are in. A geometry node, a dynamics step, a Solaris stage, a Copernicus material, a shader, or a render node reads differently, because those are different places to work.
- What is wired in, and what is not. An empty input is named, along with the help sentence for that input. What you connect is still your setup.
- Where to look in the parameter window. If the section sits under a tab, the panel names that tab. You still set the numbers and the look.
- The cook error, when there is one, next to the heading it matches. If the error does not name a heading, Gemma may add up to three sentences from `skills/houdini-context/SKILL.md`. That skill forbids invented values. A heading that is already named does not call Gemma.

Fluid, cloth, muscle, Copernicus, and Solaris are not a separate lesson pack. A Pyro solver, a cloth object, or a MaterialX node shows the section from that node's own help, placed against the wires on the node you clicked. The menu at the bottom opens another heading from the same file.

"""Parameter guide for the node that is open.

The window stays up while Houdini is used. It follows the selection.
Pictures and menu choices come from the help shipped with this install.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from houdini_wizard.context import build_study, image_bytes
from houdini_wizard.help_file import Section

_WINDOW = None
_CALLBACK = None


def show_panel(
    sections: tuple[Section, ...] | list[Section],
    scene: dict,
    focus_heading: str,
    extra_note: str = "",
    refresh=None,
) -> None:
    try:
        _qt_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note, refresh)
    except Exception:
        _plain_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note)


def _qt_panel(sections, scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str, refresh) -> None:
    try:
        from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets
    except ImportError:
        from PySide2 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets
    import hou

    study = build_study(sections, scene, focus_heading)
    if extra_note:
        study["note"] = f"{extra_note} {study['note']}".strip()

    window = _window(QtWidgets, QtCore, QtGui, hou)
    window.present(study, raise_window=True)
    _follow(hou, window, refresh)


def _window(widgets, core, gui, hou):
    global _WINDOW
    if _WINDOW is not None:
        return _WINDOW
    flags = core.Qt.Window | core.Qt.WindowMinimizeButtonHint | core.Qt.WindowMaximizeButtonHint | core.Qt.WindowCloseButtonHint
    dialog = widgets.QDialog(hou.qt.mainWindow())
    dialog.setWindowFlags(flags)
    dialog.setWindowModality(core.Qt.NonModal)
    dialog.setAttribute(core.Qt.WA_QuitOnClose, False)
    dialog.setMinimumSize(460, 320)
    dialog.resize(560, 640)
    dialog.setSizeGripEnabled(True)
    dialog.setStyleSheet(_STYLE)
    dialog._fitted = False
    dialog._gui = gui
    dialog._widgets = widgets
    dialog._core = core

    outer = widgets.QVBoxLayout(dialog)
    outer.setContentsMargins(18, 16, 18, 14)
    outer.setSpacing(8)

    dialog.scroll = widgets.QScrollArea()
    dialog.scroll.setWidgetResizable(True)
    dialog.scroll.setFrameShape(widgets.QFrame.NoFrame)
    dialog.page = widgets.QWidget()
    dialog.page_layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(dialog.page)
    dialog.page_layout.setContentsMargins(2, 2, 8, 8)
    dialog.page_layout.setSpacing(10)
    dialog.scroll.setWidget(dialog.page)
    outer.addWidget(dialog.scroll, 1)

    jump_row = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    jump_label = widgets.QLabel("Jump to a parameter")
    jump_label.setObjectName("jumpLabel")
    dialog.jump = widgets.QComboBox()
    dialog.jump.setObjectName("jump")
    jump_row.addWidget(jump_label)
    jump_row.addWidget(dialog.jump, 1)
    outer.addLayout(jump_row)
    dialog.jump.currentIndexChanged.connect(lambda index: _scroll_to(dialog, index))

    def present(study: dict, raise_window: bool) -> None:
        _fill(dialog, study)
        dialog.setWindowTitle(study.get("type_label") or "Houdini wizard")
        if not dialog._fitted:
            _fit(dialog)
            dialog._fitted = True
        if dialog.isMinimized():
            return
        dialog.show()
        if raise_window:
            dialog.raise_()
            dialog.activateWindow()

    def closeEvent(event) -> None:
        _stop_follow(hou)
        widgets.QDialog.closeEvent(dialog, event)

    dialog.present = present
    dialog.closeEvent = closeEvent
    _WINDOW = dialog
    return dialog


def _fill(dialog, study: dict) -> None:
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    layout = dialog.page_layout
    while layout.count():
        item = layout.takeAt(0)
        child = item.widget()
        if child is not None:
            child.deleteLater()
        nested = item.layout()
        if nested is not None:
            _clear_layout(nested)

    dialog._cards = []
    header = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    icon = _icon_label(dialog, study.get("icon") or "")
    if icon is not None:
        header.addWidget(icon)
    titles = widgets.QVBoxLayout()
    where = widgets.QLabel(study.get("where") or "")
    where.setObjectName("where")
    where.setWordWrap(True)
    title = widgets.QLabel(study.get("type_label") or "")
    title.setObjectName("title")
    title.setWordWrap(True)
    summary = widgets.QLabel(study.get("summary") or "")
    summary.setObjectName("summary")
    summary.setWordWrap(True)
    path = widgets.QLabel(study.get("path") or "")
    path.setObjectName("path")
    path.setWordWrap(True)
    titles.addWidget(where)
    titles.addWidget(title)
    if study.get("summary"):
        titles.addWidget(summary)
    titles.addWidget(path)
    header.addLayout(titles, 1)
    layout.addLayout(header)

    if study.get("error"):
        layout.addWidget(_callout(widgets, study["error"], "error"))
    if study.get("callout"):
        layout.addWidget(_callout(widgets, study["callout"], "callout"))
    if study.get("note"):
        note = widgets.QLabel(study["note"])
        note.setObjectName("note")
        note.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(note)

    columns = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    columns.addWidget(_ends_box(widgets, "Node input", study.get("inputs") or [], "No input on this node."))
    columns.addWidget(_ends_box(widgets, "Node output", study.get("outputs") or [], "No output on this node."))
    layout.addLayout(columns)

    if study.get("steps"):
        layout.addWidget(_section_label(widgets, "How to use it"))
        for index, step in enumerate(study["steps"], start=1):
            line = widgets.QLabel(f"{index}.  {step}")
            line.setWordWrap(True)
            line.setObjectName("step")
            layout.addWidget(line)

    if study.get("figures"):
        layout.addWidget(_section_label(widgets, "What the choices look like"))
        for figure in study["figures"]:
            layout.addWidget(_figure(dialog, figure))

    layout.addWidget(_section_label(widgets, "Parameters"))
    lead = "Each choice is quoted from this node's help. The value is still yours."
    intro = widgets.QLabel(lead)
    intro.setObjectName("intro")
    intro.setWordWrap(True)
    layout.addWidget(intro)

    folder = None
    for row in study.get("parameters") or []:
        if row.get("folder") and row["folder"] != folder:
            folder = row["folder"]
            tab = widgets.QLabel(folder)
            tab.setObjectName("folder")
            layout.addWidget(tab)
        card = _parameter(widgets, row)
        dialog._cards.append(card)
        layout.addWidget(card)

    if not study.get("parameters"):
        empty = widgets.QLabel("This help file has no parameter list.")
        empty.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(empty)

    if study.get("next_groups"):
        layout.addWidget(_section_label(widgets, "Continue with"))
        hint = widgets.QLabel("Select the next node and this window follows it.")
        hint.setObjectName("intro")
        hint.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(hint)
        for group in study["next_groups"]:
            names = widgets.QLabel("   ".join(group["names"]))
            names.setObjectName("nextNames")
            names.setWordWrap(True)
            why = widgets.QLabel(group["why"])
            why.setObjectName("nextWhy")
            why.setWordWrap(True)
            layout.addWidget(names)
            layout.addWidget(why)

    if study.get("cache"):
        layout.addWidget(_section_label(widgets, "Keep working while it cooks"))
        cache = widgets.QLabel(study["cache"])
        cache.setObjectName("cache")
        cache.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(cache)

    layout.addStretch(1)

    dialog.jump.blockSignals(True)
    dialog.jump.clear()
    for row in study.get("parameters") or []:
        label = f"{row['folder']}  /  {row['name']}" if row.get("folder") else row["name"]
        dialog.jump.addItem(label)
    selected = next((index for index, row in enumerate(study.get("parameters") or []) if row.get("selected")), 0)
    if dialog.jump.count():
        dialog.jump.setCurrentIndex(selected)
    dialog.jump.blockSignals(False)
    if study.get("parameters") and any(row.get("selected") for row in study["parameters"]):
        _scroll_to(dialog, selected)


def _parameter(widgets, row: dict):
    card = widgets.QFrame()
    card.setObjectName("selected" if row.get("selected") else "parm")
    layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(card)
    layout.setContentsMargins(12, 8, 12, 8)
    layout.setSpacing(4)
    title = widgets.QLabel(row["name"])
    title.setObjectName("parmName")
    layout.addWidget(title)
    if row.get("meaning"):
        meaning = widgets.QLabel(row["meaning"])
        meaning.setObjectName("meaning")
        meaning.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(meaning)
    if row.get("current"):
        now = widgets.QLabel(f"Now: {row['current']}")
        now.setObjectName("now")
        now.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(now)
    for option in row.get("options") or []:
        text = option["name"]
        if option.get("meaning"):
            text = f"{option['name']}  —  {option['meaning']}"
        if option.get("current"):
            text = f"Now   {text}"
        line = widgets.QLabel(text)
        line.setObjectName("optionNow" if option.get("current") else "option")
        line.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(line)
    return card


def _figure(dialog, figure: dict):
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    box = widgets.QWidget()
    layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(box)
    layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    layout.setSpacing(4)
    if figure.get("label"):
        label = widgets.QLabel(figure["label"])
        label.setObjectName("figureLabel")
        layout.addWidget(label)
    row = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    shown = False
    for path in figure.get("images") or []:
        pixmap = _pixmap(dialog, path)
        if pixmap is None:
            continue
        shown = True
        pic = widgets.QLabel()
        pic.setPixmap(pixmap)
        row.addWidget(pic)
    row.addStretch(1)
    if shown:
        layout.addLayout(row)
    return box


def _pixmap(dialog, path: str):
    data = image_bytes(dialog._study_hfs if hasattr(dialog, "_study_hfs") else "", path)
    return None


def _load_pixmap(dialog, hfs: str, path: str):
    gui = dialog._gui
    core = dialog._core
    data = image_bytes(hfs, path)
    if not data:
        return None
    image = gui.QImage.fromData(data)
    if image.isNull():
        return None
    pixmap = gui.QPixmap.fromImage(image)
    return pixmap.scaledToHeight(120, core.Qt.SmoothTransformation)


def _figure_pixmaps(dialog, hfs: str, figure: dict):
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    box = widgets.QWidget()
    layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(box)
    layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    layout.setSpacing(4)
    if figure.get("label"):
        label = widgets.QLabel(figure["label"])
        label.setObjectName("figureLabel")
        layout.addWidget(label)
    row = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    shown = False
    for path in figure.get("images") or []:
        pixmap = _load_pixmap(dialog, hfs, path)
        if pixmap is None:
            continue
        shown = True
        pic = widgets.QLabel()
        pic.setPixmap(pixmap)
        row.addWidget(pic)
    row.addStretch(1)
    if shown:
        layout.addLayout(row)
    return box


def _icon_label(dialog, name: str):
    if not name:
        return None
    try:
        import hou

        icon = hou.qt.Icon(name, 28, 28)
        pixmap = icon.pixmap(28, 28)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if pixmap.isNull():
        return None
    label = dialog._widgets.QLabel()
    label.setPixmap(pixmap)
    label.setFixedSize(32, 32)
    return label


def _ends_box(widgets, title: str, rows: list[dict], empty: str):
    box = widgets.QGroupBox(title)
    layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(box)
    if not rows:
        label = widgets.QLabel(empty)
        label.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(label)
        return box
    for row in rows:
        state = row["state"]
        text = row["label"] if not state else f"{row['label']}: {state}"
        label = widgets.QLabel(text)
        label.setObjectName("wire")
        label.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(label)
        if row.get("meaning"):
            meaning = widgets.QLabel(row["meaning"])
            meaning.setObjectName("meaning")
            meaning.setWordWrap(True)
            layout.addWidget(meaning)
    return box


def _callout(widgets, text: str, name: str):
    label = widgets.QLabel(text)
    label.setObjectName(name)
    label.setWordWrap(True)
    return label


def _section_label(widgets, text: str):
    label = widgets.QLabel(text)
    label.setObjectName("section")
    return label


def _scroll_to(dialog, index: int) -> None:
    cards = getattr(dialog, "_cards", [])
    if index < 0 or index >= len(cards):
        return
    dialog.scroll.ensureWidgetVisible(cards[index], 0, 40)


def _fit(dialog) -> None:
    screen = dialog.screen()
    if screen is None:
        dialog.resize(560, 640)
        return
    area = screen.availableGeometry()
    dialog.resize(min(620, int(area.width() * 0.38)), min(760, int(area.height() * 0.72)))


def _clear_layout(layout) -> None:
    while layout.count():
        item = layout.takeAt(0)
        child = item.widget()
        if child is not None:
            child.deleteLater()
        nested = item.layout()
        if nested is not None:
            _clear_layout(nested)


def _follow(hou, window, refresh) -> None:
    global _CALLBACK
    if refresh is None or not hasattr(hou.ui, "addEventLoopCallback"):
        return
    if _CALLBACK is not None:
        return

    def tick() -> None:
        if _WINDOW is None or not _WINDOW.isVisible():
            _stop_follow(hou)
            return
        try:
            payload = refresh()
        except Exception:
            return
        if not payload:
            return
        sections, scene, focus, extra = payload
        study = build_study(sections, scene, focus)
        if extra:
            study["note"] = f"{extra} {study['note']}".strip()
        window._study_hfs = study.get("hfs") or ""
        window.present(study, raise_window=False)

    _CALLBACK = tick
    hou.ui.addEventLoopCallback(tick)


def _stop_follow(hou) -> None:
    global _CALLBACK
    callback = _CALLBACK
    _CALLBACK = None
    if callback is None:
        return
    try:
        hou.ui.removeEventLoopCallback(callback)
    except Exception:
        pass


def _plain_panel(sections, scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str) -> None:
    import hou

    study = build_study(sections, scene, focus_heading)
    lines = [study.get("where") or "", study.get("summary") or "", study.get("error") or "", extra_note, study.get("note") or ""]
    for row in study.get("parameters") or []:
        lines.append(row["name"])
        if row.get("meaning"):
            lines.append(row["meaning"])
        for option in row.get("options") or []:
            lines.append(f"{option['name']}: {option['meaning']}")
    text = "\n\n".join(part for part in lines if part)
    hou.ui.displayMessage(text, title=study.get("type_label") or "Houdini wizard")


_STYLE = """
QDialog { background: #241f1b; color: #f4efe6; }
QScrollArea, QWidget { background: #241f1b; color: #f4efe6; }
QLabel { color: #f4efe6; font-size: 13px; }
QLabel#where { color: #d7a15a; font-size: 12px; }

content.text:
The panel is now a parameter guide for the node you have selected, and it stays open while you keep working in Houdini.

Restart Houdini, then click **Section card** on something like UV Unwrap or UV Project. What you should see:

* **Parameters** are the main section. Each one has the sentence from this install’s help. A menu lists every choice with the result that sentence describes. UV Unwrap’s Layout shows Strip and Square. Scale shows None, Uniform, and Stretch. The choice currently set on the node is marked **Now**. The window does not type a value for you.
* **What the choices look like** uses the pictures already shipped with the help. On UV Project that is Orthographic, Polar, Cylindrical, Toroidal, and Plastic Wrap.
* **Node input** and **Node output** replace the old wire labels, including when nothing is connected.
* **Jump to a parameter** is the label on the dropdown.
* **Continue with** names the next nodes the help itself mentions, such as UV Edit or UV Fuse. Select one of those and the same window follows it.
* **Keep working while it cooks** tells you to put a File Cache after a node that is too slow to adjust around. It does not pick a number. If the node already has its own cache or freeze parameter, the panel points at that instead.

The window is no longer a blocking dialog. You can move it, resize it, or minimize it and keep using Houdini. It updates when you select a different node or parameter. A speed or quality tradeoff appears only when that node’s own help says it. The panel will not guess that one menu choice is faster than another.

🌐 Community Wisdom
🧭 [GuideAgent — A Lightweight SDK to Guide Users Inside Web Apps](https://dev.to/raghul_r29/-guideagent-a-lightweight-sdk-to-guide-users-inside-web-apps-52i8) 👤 [@raghul_r29](https://dev.to/raghul_r29) — Guide people inside the tool they are already using, which is this window sitting on the live node instead of a separate help page. 🔗 [Read Full Discussion on DEV](https://dev.to/raghul_r29/-guideagent-a-lightweight-sdk-to-guide-users-inside-web-apps-52i8)

"""Parameter guide for the node that is open.

The window stays up while Houdini is used. It follows the selection.
Pictures, menu choices, and number ranges come from this install.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from houdini_wizard.context import build_study, image_bytes
from houdini_wizard.help_file import Section

_WINDOW = None
_CALLBACK = None


def show_panel(
    sections: tuple[Section, ...] | list[Section],
    scene: dict,
    focus_heading: str,
    extra_note: str = "",
    refresh=None,
) -> None:
    try:
        _qt_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note, refresh)
    except Exception:
        _plain_panel(sections, scene, focus_heading, extra_note)


def _qt_panel(sections, scene: dict, focus_heading: str, extra_note: str, refresh) -> None:
    try:
        from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets
    except ImportError:
        from PySide2 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets
    import hou

    study = build_study(sections, scene, focus_heading)
    if extra_note:
        study["note"] = f"{extra_note} {study['note']}".strip()

    window = _window(QtWidgets, QtCore, QtGui, hou)
    window.present(study, raise_window=True)
    _follow(hou, window, refresh)


def _window(widgets, core, gui, hou):
    global _WINDOW
    if _WINDOW is not None:
        return _WINDOW
    flags = core.Qt.Window | core.Qt.WindowMinimizeButtonHint | core.Qt.WindowMaximizeButtonHint | core.Qt.WindowCloseButtonHint
    dialog = widgets.QDialog(hou.qt.mainWindow())
    dialog.setWindowFlags(flags)
    dialog.setWindowModality(core.Qt.NonModal)
    dialog.setAttribute(core.Qt.WA_QuitOnClose, False)
    dialog.setMinimumSize(720, 360)
    dialog.resize(960, 720)
    dialog.setSizeGripEnabled(True)
    dialog._fitted = False
    dialog._gui = gui
    dialog._widgets = widgets
    dialog._core = core
    dialog._zoom = 1.0
    dialog._theme = "dark"
    dialog._study = None
    dialog._anchors = {}
    dialog._folder_index = {}
    dialog._parm_folder = {}
    dialog.tabs = None

    outer = widgets.QVBoxLayout(dialog)
    outer.setContentsMargins(12, 10, 12, 10)
    outer.setSpacing(8)

    bar = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    dialog.zoom_out = widgets.QPushButton("A−")
    dialog.zoom_out.setToolTip("Smaller text")
    dialog.zoom_label = widgets.QLabel("100%")
    dialog.zoom_label.setObjectName("zoom")
    dialog.zoom_in = widgets.QPushButton("A+")
    dialog.zoom_in.setToolTip("Larger text")
    dialog.theme_button = widgets.QPushButton("Light")
    dialog.theme_button.setToolTip("Switch the panel colors")
    dialog.close_button = widgets.QPushButton("Exit")
    dialog.close_button.setToolTip("Close the panel")
    bar.addWidget(dialog.zoom_out)
    bar.addWidget(dialog.zoom_label)
    bar.addWidget(dialog.zoom_in)
    bar.addStretch(1)
    bar.addWidget(dialog.theme_button)
    bar.addWidget(dialog.close_button)
    outer.addLayout(bar)
    dialog.zoom_out.clicked.connect(lambda: _nudge_zoom(dialog, 1 / 1.1))
    dialog.zoom_in.clicked.connect(lambda: _nudge_zoom(dialog, 1.1))
    dialog.theme_button.clicked.connect(lambda: _toggle_theme(dialog))
    dialog.close_button.clicked.connect(dialog.close)

    body = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    body.setSpacing(12)
    dialog.outline = widgets.QListWidget()
    dialog.outline.setObjectName("outline")
    dialog.outline.setFixedWidth(210)
    dialog.outline.setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(core.Qt.ScrollBarAlwaysOff)
    dialog.outline.setFrameShape(widgets.QFrame.NoFrame)
    body.addWidget(dialog.outline)
    dialog.outline.currentRowChanged.connect(lambda row: _on_outline(dialog, row))

    dialog.scroll = widgets.QScrollArea()
    dialog.scroll.setWidgetResizable(True)
    dialog.scroll.setFrameShape(widgets.QFrame.NoFrame)
    dialog.scroll.setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(core.Qt.ScrollBarAlwaysOff)
    dialog.page = widgets.QWidget()
    dialog.page.setObjectName("page")
    dialog.page_layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(dialog.page)
    dialog.page_layout.setContentsMargins(2, 2, 8, 8)
    dialog.page_layout.setSpacing(10)
    dialog.scroll.setWidget(dialog.page)
    body.addWidget(dialog.scroll, 1)
    outer.addLayout(body, 1)

    def present(study: dict, raise_window: bool) -> None:
        previous = dialog._study
        reveal = raise_window or _selected_name(previous) != _selected_name(study)
        dialog._study = study
        _fill(dialog, study, reveal=reveal)
        dialog.setWindowTitle(study.get("type_label") or "Houdini wizard")
        if not dialog._fitted:
            _fit(dialog)
            dialog._fitted = True
        if dialog.isMinimized():
            return
        dialog.show()
        if raise_window:
            dialog.raise_()
            dialog.activateWindow()

    def closeEvent(event) -> None:
        _stop_follow(hou)
        widgets.QDialog.closeEvent(dialog, event)

    dialog.present = present
    dialog.closeEvent = closeEvent
    _restyle(dialog)
    _WINDOW = dialog
    return dialog


def _fill(dialog, study: dict, reveal: bool = False) -> None:
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    layout = dialog.page_layout
    while layout.count():
        item = layout.takeAt(0)
        child = item.widget()
        if child is not None:
            child.deleteLater()
        nested = item.layout()
        if nested is not None:
            _clear_layout(nested)

    dialog._anchors = {}
    dialog._folder_index = {}
    dialog._parm_folder = {}
    dialog.tabs = None
    dialog.outline.blockSignals(True)
    dialog.outline.clear()

    header = widgets.QWidget()
    header_layout = widgets.QHBoxLayout(header)
    header_layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    icon = _icon_label(dialog, study.get("icon") or "")
    if icon is not None:
        header_layout.addWidget(icon)
    titles = widgets.QVBoxLayout()
    where = widgets.QLabel(study.get("where") or "")
    where.setObjectName("where")
    where.setWordWrap(True)
    title = widgets.QLabel(study.get("type_label") or "")
    title.setObjectName("title")
    title.setWordWrap(True)
    summary = widgets.QLabel(study.get("summary") or "")
    summary.setObjectName("summary")
    summary.setWordWrap(True)
    path = widgets.QLabel(study.get("path") or "")
    path.setObjectName("path")
    path.setWordWrap(True)
    titles.addWidget(where)
    titles.addWidget(title)
    if study.get("summary"):
        titles.addWidget(summary)
    titles.addWidget(path)
    header_layout.addLayout(titles, 1)
    layout.addWidget(header)
    _mark(dialog, "section:overview", header, "Overview")

    if study.get("error"):
        layout.addWidget(_callout(widgets, study["error"], "error"))
    if study.get("callout"):
        layout.addWidget(_callout(widgets, study["callout"], "callout"))
    if study.get("note"):
        note = widgets.QLabel(study["note"])
        note.setObjectName("note")
        note.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(note)

    wire_host = widgets.QWidget()
    columns = widgets.QHBoxLayout(wire_host)
    columns.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    columns.addWidget(_ends_box(widgets, "Node input", study.get("inputs") or [], "No input on this node."))
    columns.addWidget(_ends_box(widgets, "Node output", study.get("outputs") or [], "No output on this node."))
    layout.addWidget(wire_host)
    _mark(dialog, "section:wires", wire_host, "Node input")

    if study.get("steps"):
        heading = _section_label(widgets, "How to use it")
        layout.addWidget(heading)
        _mark(dialog, "section:steps", heading, "How to use it")
        for index, step in enumerate(study["steps"], start=1):
            line = widgets.QLabel(f"{index}.  {step}")
            line.setWordWrap(True)
            line.setObjectName("step")
            layout.addWidget(line)

    if study.get("figures"):
        heading = _section_label(widgets, "What the choices look like")
        layout.addWidget(heading)
        _mark(dialog, "section:figures", heading, "Pictures")
        for figure in study["figures"]:
            layout.addWidget(_figure_pixmaps(dialog, study.get("hfs") or "", figure))

    heading = _section_label(widgets, "Parameters")
    layout.addWidget(heading)
    _mark(dialog, "section:parameters", heading, "Parameters")
    intro = widgets.QLabel("The parameters of this node are listed below. A guide to adjusting their values is included.")
    intro.setObjectName("intro")
    intro.setWordWrap(True)
    layout.addWidget(intro)

    groups = _groups(study.get("parameters") or [])
    chosen = ""
    if len(groups) > 1:
        dialog.tabs = widgets.QTabWidget()
        dialog.tabs.setDocumentMode(True)
        for index, (folder, rows) in enumerate(groups):
            page = widgets.QWidget()
            page_layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(page)
            page_layout.setContentsMargins(8, 8, 8, 8)
            page_layout.setSpacing(8)
            for row in rows:
                card = _parameter(widgets, row)
                page_layout.addWidget(card)
                key = f"parm:{row['name']}"
                dialog._anchors[key] = card
                dialog._parm_folder[key] = folder
                _outline_item(dialog, key, row["name"], 1)
                if row.get("selected"):
                    chosen = key
            page_layout.addStretch(1)
            label = folder or "Main"
            dialog.tabs.addTab(page, label)
            dialog._folder_index[folder] = index
            _outline_item(dialog, f"folder:{folder}", label, 0)
        dialog._anchors["section:parameters"] = dialog.tabs
        layout.addWidget(dialog.tabs)
        if chosen:
            dialog.tabs.setCurrentIndex(dialog._folder_index.get(dialog._parm_folder.get(chosen, ""), 0))
    else:
        rows = groups[0][1] if groups else []
        for row in rows:
            card = _parameter(widgets, row)
            layout.addWidget(card)
            key = f"parm:{row['name']}"
            dialog._anchors[key] = card
            dialog._parm_folder[key] = ""
            _outline_item(dialog, key, row["name"], 1)
            if row.get("selected"):
                chosen = key
        if not rows:
            empty = widgets.QLabel("This help file has no parameter list.")
            empty.setWordWrap(True)
            layout.addWidget(empty)

    if study.get("next_groups"):
        heading = _section_label(widgets, "Continue with")
        layout.addWidget(heading)
        _mark(dialog, "section:next", heading, "Continue with")

            "These are nodes the help places next to this one. "
            "The note under each name says what that node is for, so you can choose which part of the setup to build next."

        hint.setObjectName("intro")
        hint.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(hint)
        for group in study["next_groups"]:
            names = widgets.QLabel("   ".join(group["names"]))
            names.setObjectName("nextNames")
            names.setWordWrap(True)

            why.setObjectName("nextWhy")
            why.setWordWrap(True)
            layout.addWidget(names)
            layout.addWidget(why)

    if study.get("cache"):
        heading = _section_label(widgets, "Keep working while it cooks")
        layout.addWidget(heading)
        _mark(dialog, "section:cache", heading, "Keep working")

    layout.addStretch(1)

        _activate(dialog, chosen)


def _groups(parameters: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]:
    groups: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]] = []
    for row in parameters:
        folder = row.get("folder") or ""
        if not groups or groups[-1][0] != folder:
            groups.append((folder, []))
        groups[-1][1].append(row)
    return groups


def _mark(dialog, key: str, widget, label: str, depth: int = 0) -> None:
    dialog._anchors[key] = widget
    _outline_item(dialog, key, label, depth)


def _outline_item(dialog, key: str, label: str, depth: int) -> None:
    item = dialog._widgets.QListWidgetItem(("    " * depth) + label)
    item.setData(dialog._core.Qt.UserRole, key)
    dialog.outline.addItem(item)


def _on_outline(dialog, row: int) -> None:
    if row < 0:
        return
    item = dialog.outline.item(row)
    if item is None:
        return
    _activate(dialog, item.data(dialog._core.Qt.UserRole))


def _activate(dialog, key: str) -> None:
    if not key:
        return
    if key.startswith("folder:"):
        folder = key.split(":", 1)[1]
        if dialog.tabs is not None and folder in dialog._folder_index:
            dialog.tabs.setCurrentIndex(dialog._folder_index[folder])
        target = dialog.tabs
    else:
        folder = dialog._parm_folder.get(key, "")
        if folder and dialog.tabs is not None and folder in dialog._folder_index:
            dialog.tabs.setCurrentIndex(dialog._folder_index[folder])
        target = dialog._anchors.get(key)
    if target is not None:
        dialog.scroll.ensureWidgetVisible(target, 0, 28)

    card = widgets.QFrame()

        meaning.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(meaning)
    if row.get("range"):
        span = widgets.QLabel(row["range"])
        span.setObjectName("range")
        span.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(span)
    if row.get("current") and not any(option.get("current") for option in row.get("options") or []):
        now = widgets.QLabel(f"Now: {row['current']}")
        now.setObjectName("now")
        now.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(now)

def _load_pixmap(dialog, hfs: str, path: str):
    gui = dialog._gui
    core = dialog._core
    data = image_bytes(hfs, path)
    if not data:
        return None
    image = gui.QImage.fromData(data)
    if image.isNull():
        return None
    pixmap = gui.QPixmap.fromImage(image)
    height = max(96, int(180 * getattr(dialog, "_zoom", 1.0)))
    try:
        return pixmap.scaledToHeight(height, core.Qt.SmoothTransformation)
    except Exception:
        return pixmap.scaledToHeight(height)


def _figure_pixmaps(dialog, hfs: str, figure: dict):
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    box = widgets.QWidget()
    layout = widgets.QVBoxLayout(box)
    layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    layout.setSpacing(4)
    if figure.get("label"):
        label = widgets.QLabel(figure["label"])
        label.setObjectName("figureLabel")
        layout.addWidget(label)
    row = widgets.QHBoxLayout()
    shown = False
    for path in figure.get("images") or []:
        pixmap = _load_pixmap(dialog, hfs, path)
        if pixmap is None:
            continue
        shown = True
        pic = widgets.QLabel()
        pic.setPixmap(pixmap)
        row.addWidget(pic)
    row.addStretch(1)
    if shown:
        layout.addLayout(row)
    return box


def _icon_label(dialog, name: str):

    try:

        icon = hou.qt.Icon(name, 28, 28)

    except Exception:

    if pixmap.isNull():

    label = dialog._widgets.QLabel()

    label.setFixedSize(32, 32)

def _follow(hou, window, refresh) -> None:
    global _CALLBACK
    if refresh is None or not hasattr(hou.ui, "addEventLoopCallback"):
        return
    if _CALLBACK is not None:
        return

    def tick() -> None:
        if _WINDOW is None or not _WINDOW.isVisible():
            _stop_follow(hou)
            return
        try:
            payload = refresh()
        except Exception:
            return
        if not payload:
            return
        sections, scene, focus, extra = payload
        study = build_study(sections, scene, focus)
        if extra:
            study["note"] = f"{extra} {study['note']}".strip()
        window.present(study, raise_window=False)

    _CALLBACK = tick
    try:
        hou.ui.addEventLoopCallback(tick)
    except Exception:
        _CALLBACK = None


def _stop_follow(hou) -> None:
    global _CALLBACK
    callback = _CALLBACK
    _CALLBACK = None
    if callback is None:
        return
    try:
        hou.ui.removeEventLoopCallback(callback)
    except Exception:
        pass

    hou.ui.displayMessage(text, title=study.get("type_label") or "Houdini wizard")

content.text:
Clicking empty space in Houdini no longer opens that "Select a node" dialog. The panel stays on the last node until you select another one.

Restart Houdini and open the panel again. The top bar is always there: **A−** and **A+** scale the text, **Light** or **Dark** switches the colors, and **Exit** closes the panel. Text is resized as text, so it stays sharp. Pictures are drawn larger, and they scale with that same control.

The left column is a list of sections, in place of the unlabeled dropdown. On a node with several parameter tabs, such as UV Project, those tabs are separate: Main, Transformation, Initialize, and so on. A parameter that sits outside a tab is not pulled into the previous one.

Number parameters now include the range from that parameter's own slider. A closed 0 to 1 range says to pick 0 for the least of what the line above describes, and 1 for the most. If the slider is only a guide, the line says you can type outside it. Menu parameters still list each choice and what the help says it does. The panel does not invent a third value or a look.

arguments.body_markdown:
You already have the node selected. Houdini's help still opens at the top of the article. It does not know that the first input is empty, or that Distribution is already set to Gaussian. I built a shelf tool that stays on that node and uses the help file that shipped with this install.

## What I Built

houdini-wizard is a shelf tool. You click it with a node selected, and a window stays open while you keep working in the network. You can minimize it. It follows the next node you select.

The window is the help for that node, arranged so a parameter is easier to read. Inputs and outputs show what is connected. Parameters sit in the same folders Houdini uses. If the tooltip already tells you what raising the value does, that sentence stays. I add the slider's own ends next to it, so the range is sitting with the words you already trust.

A menu stays a menu. None, Uniform, Gaussian, and Log Normal are the choices from the help file, with the sentence that file gives each one. I do not pick one for the shot.

## Demo

On Ocean Spectrum, Wind Speed already says that higher wind speeds create larger low-frequency waves. The window keeps that sentence and writes the range in front of it. Gemma is not called.

Rotate is different. Its help is four words: rotate angles in degrees. That is the kind of short label the window will ask Gemma to turn into one sentence. Zero means no rotation. Positive and negative values turn opposite ways. The help does not say clockwise, so the sentence does not say clockwise either.

If a cook error names a heading, the window quotes that section and skips the model. If the error does not name one, Gemma picks a heading from the file, or says none of them match. The body of the card is still the file's own text.

## Code

The gate is small. A tip that already explains the result, or that is long enough to read, never goes to the model.

```python
def _needs_model(meaning: str) -> bool:
    if _effect_clause(meaning):
        return False
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9']+", meaning)
    return len(words) <= 6
```

`_effect_clause` looks for the words the help already uses, such as higher, lower, increasing, or slower. Wind Speed has "higher", so it stops there.

## How I Built It

Gemma 3 4B runs locally through Ollama. It is not an agent loop. Two skills are handed to it as extra instructions, because a normal chat does not follow them.

One skill is only for a cook error that does not name a heading. Gemma returns one heading from the list, or none. The shelf then quotes that section from the help that shipped with this Houdini. It does not ask the model to write the paragraph.

The other skill is the short value line. It is sent a name, the help sentence, and the slider ends. It may return one sentence. A number that is not the low end, the high end, zero, or already in the help is thrown away.

Temporal is one Python workflow. It retries that heading pick, and if Houdini quits, the same card comes back for that node. A new cook error is a new card, because the node in front of you changed.

Entire sits beside the build. I use it to search why the shelf skips Gemma when a heading is already named. It is not called when you click the shelf.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  activeNode["active network node"] --> wizard["houdini-wizard shelf"]
  wizard --> helpFile["installed help file"]
  helpFile --> gemma["Gemma picks one heading"]
  gemma --> quote["wizard quotes that help section"]
  gemma --> noMatch["no match lists headings the user can open"]
  quote --> temporal["Temporal workflow keeps this card"]
  noMatch --> temporal
  temporal --> updated["user updates the active node"]
```

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter

The useful file is the one in this Houdini. A page on the web can describe a different build, and a cloud model can remember a parameter that this node does not have. Running an open-weight model next to the help that shipped with the software is what keeps the quote honest. You still change the node. The window does not set a value, a flag, or a wire.

## Agent session

{% embed https://dev.to/agent_sessions/houdini-section-card-dbmcoa %}

## Prize Categories

Gemma, Temporal, and Entire.

content.text:
Gemma only rewrites a tip when it is a short label and does not already say what the number does. A tip that already explains the result stays, with the slider’s own ends written in front of it.

**Left as the tooltip.** Ocean Spectrum, Wind Speed. The help already says “Higher wind speeds create larger low-frequency waves.” The window keeps that sentence and only adds the range the slider reports, for example “Wind Speed from 0 to 10, or greater than 10.” Distribution stays the menu from the file: None, Uniform, Gaussian, Log Normal, each with its own sentence. Size of a box is the same kind of line. It already says what it is, so it is not sent to the model.

**The one short line Gemma may write.** Rotate, whose help is only “Rotate angles in degrees,” with a slider from 0 to 360. That is four words and no result, so it is the case the model is for. An allowed sentence is: “Rotate angles in degrees, from 0 to 360, or past 360. 0 means no rotation. Positive and negative values turn opposite ways.” A sentence that adds clockwise, or a number the help never gave, is thrown away. Until that reply comes back, the same shape is shown from the help and the slider, so the window is never waiting on the model to be readable.

That gate is now in the shelf. A tip is sent to Gemma only when it has no result words such as higher, lower, increasing, or slower, and it is six words or fewer. Restart Houdini so this copy loads.

Yes. FLIP was only the check. The same rule covers the other solvers in this Houdini.

A related node is read from the link on that page, so a Pyro Solver can list both DOP and SOP pages, and Vellum, Cloth, FEM, Smoke, Whitewater, and MPM do the same. POP Solver and the DOP Bullet Solver have no related list in the installed help, so the section stays empty for them.

The cache note follows the network the solver lives in:

- A solver in a dynamics network, including Pyro, Vellum, POP, Cloth, FEM, Smoke, Whitewater, Bullet, and MPM, gets the simulation-cache line.
- A solver in a geometry network that already has its own cache control uses that control. The SOP Pyro Solver and Tissue Solver point at **Cache Simulation**. The SOP Vellum Solver points at **Cache Enabled**. MPM, RBD Bullet, Whitewater, and the SOP FLIP Solver are handled the same way when their help page names a cache parameter.

There is no separate sentence written for each solver. The page’s own help decides which of those two notes you see.

def _groups(parameters: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]:
    """One tab per top-level folder. Nested folders stay inside that tab."""
    groups: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]] = []
    for row in parameters:
        path = tuple(row.get("groups") or ())
        folder = path[0] if path else (row.get("folder") or "")
        if not groups or groups[-1][0] != folder:
            groups.append((folder, []))
        groups[-1][1].append(row)
    return groups


def _add_parameters(dialog, layout, rows: list[dict], tab) -> str:
    """Lay parameters in pane order, with a heading for each nested folder."""
    widgets = dialog._widgets
    chosen = ""
    shown: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    for row in rows:
        path = tuple(row.get("groups") or ())
        nested = path[1:]
        shared = 0
        while shared < len(shown) and shared < len(nested) and shown[shared] == nested[shared]:
            shared += 1
        for index in range(shared, len(nested)):
            head = widgets.QLabel(nested[index])
            head.setObjectName("folderHead")
            head.setContentsMargins((index + 1) * 14, 10, 0, 0)
            layout.addWidget(head)
            _outline_item(dialog, f"folder:{tab}:{nested[index]}", nested[index], index + 1)
        shown = nested
        depth = len(nested)
        card = _parameter(widgets, row, depth)
        layout.addWidget(card)
        key = f"parm:{row['name']}:{path}"
        dialog._anchors[key] = card
        dialog._parm_folder[key] = tab
        _outline_item(dialog, key, row["name"], depth + 1)
        if row.get("selected"):
            chosen = key
    return chosen

    """Open the help page as a new tab in the help browser, not a new window."""

content.text:
The Use with names now open a **new tab in Houdini’s help browser**. The first click places that browser tab. Each later click adds another tab in the same browser, rather than a separate window. The old click was looking for a help call this Houdini does not put on `hou.ui`, so it returned without opening anything.

On UV Layout the parameter tabs now follow the parameter pane. **Islands To Pack** is one tab. Inside it, Overrides is a heading, and Connectivity, Target assignment, Variable scaling, and Projection offset sit under that heading with their settings indented beneath them. Scale Island and Axis Alignment stay in Islands To Pack, after Overrides. The other tabs are Packing, Targets, Island Stacking, and Output Groups and Attributes. Advanced stays inside Packing. Menu choices are listed as bullets under the parameter they belong to.

The theme toggle and the zoom controls restyle the page that is already open, so the scroll position stays where you left it. The content scrollbar thumb is a light bar on the dark background. Loading is lighter too: the help archive stays open for the related pages, and a theme or zoom change no longer rebuilds every card.

Restart Houdini so this copy loads.

Keeping your place when the view changes is the same problem Prince Kukreja describes in [Preserving Scroll State on Tab Change in Angular](https://dev.to/princekukreja/preserving-scroll-state-on-tab-change-in-angular-3l92). The theme switch now leaves the scrollbar alone for that reason.
but the parameter tabs are not just for the UV layout, any other complex variety of nodes would need to use that system to follow their respective parameter pane content
The nesting already comes from each node’s own help headings, not from a UV Layout list. I’ll check a few other complex nodes and make sure their parameter panes drive the tabs the same way.

Every node uses that same folder reading. UV Layout was only the one on screen.

The shelf reads the help file for the node you have selected. Each `==` heading in that file becomes a tab. A `===` or `====` heading stays inside the tab above it, in the same order as that node’s parameter pane. A node with no folders, such as Box or UV Unwrap, stays one list.

On this Houdini that produces:

- **Vellum Solver:** Solver, Forces, Simulation, Advanced, Visualize. Collisions stays inside Solver.
- **Pyro Solver:** Setup, Bounds, Collision, Sourcing, Fields, Shape, Look, Advanced.
- **RBD Bullet Solver:** folders three levels deep, such as Guide, then Enable Guides, then Guide Blending.
- **FLIP Solver:** Substeps, Particle Motion, Volume Motion, Narrow Band, Distribution. Behavior stays inside Particle Motion.
- **Principled Shader:** Surface, Opacity, Textures, Bump and Normals, Displacement, Settings. Reflection stays inside Surface, then Specular.

If you've ever used Houdini for VFX, Procedural modelling, animation or CG  content creation then you're probably familiar with its help-browser. Houdini's help-browser is a very useful source of documentation for any user looking for more information about all parts of Houdini. However, It is not context-aware, and does not know how a user's node networks are wired, or what parameter settings have been applied to a given or selected node. I built a new shelf tool that stays on that displays more details about actively selected nodes and uses the currently installed local-help file that shipped with the user's version of Houdini.

## What I Built

houdini-wizard is a super-charged help-browser shelf tool. With any node selected, it will display organised documentation that updates based on what node is actively selected in the node network viewer. You can continue work in the network panel, while the tool is open and it will keep updating its help information or minimise it to avoid taking up screen-space.

**The coolest features this tool has that you won't find in a standard help-browser:**

- Update help documentation for newly selected nodes.
- Shows node's Input and Output connection status.
- Adopts Houdini's existing Parameter organisation.
- Enriches Parameter documentation by including their tooltips, keeping all this info in one panel and not just in the UI.
- Maintains existing UI helper-text that users can access on-hover of parameter settings.

The code is on GitHub: [houdini-wizard](https://github.com/AbisoyeOnanuga/houdini-wizard).

## Demo

A node in Houdini is one box in the network. It has settings, called parameters, and a short hover tip on each one. When Houdini tries to compute that node and fails, you get a cook error. The help browser can explain the node type. It does not know which setting you are hovering, or which wire is empty, or which sentence in the error matches a heading in the manual.

Take a node that builds an ocean. Its Wind Speed tip already says that higher wind speeds create larger, low-frequency waves. The window keeps that sentence. It only writes the slider's real range in front of it, so you can see the numbers beside words you already trust. There is nothing for a model to invent there.

Rotate is the opposite kind of tip. The manual says "rotate angles in degrees," and that is almost the whole sentence. You can see a slider from 0 to 360, but the tip never says what 0 means. This is the one place the window asks Gemma for a single line: 0 means no rotation, and positive and negative values turn opposite ways. The manual never says clockwise, so the line does not say clockwise either.

A cook error is the same idea. If the error already names a parameter, the window quotes that section and leaves the model alone. If the error is vague, Gemma's only job is to point at one heading that already exists in the file, or to say that none of them match. The paragraph you read is still the manual that shipped with your Houdini.

## Code

Most parameters never reach the model. The check is small on purpose. If the help already uses a word like higher, lower, increasing, or slower, the tip has told you what changing the number does. A longer tip is also left alone. Only a short label, about six words, with no result in it, is sent on.

```python
def _needs_model(meaning: str) -> bool:
    if _effect_clause(meaning):
        return False
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9']+", meaning)
    return len(words) <= 6
```

Wind Speed contains "higher," so it stops here. "Rotate angles in degrees" does not, so it can go through.

## How I Built It

The shelf button is the part you click. These are the pieces behind it, and the job each one actually has.

**Houdini's installed help.** Every quote starts from the help files in this install, the same manual your build already uses. A page from the website can describe a different version. The file on disk cannot.

**Houdini Python.** The shelf is a Python script Houdini runs in-process. It can see the node you selected, which inputs are connected, and which parameter is current. That is what makes the window follow the network instead of opening one generic article.

**Gemma 3 4B, through Ollama.** Gemma is a small open model, and Ollama runs it on the same machine as Houdini. I gave it two jobs, because those are the two moments the manual is not enough on its own. If a cook error does not name a heading, Gemma picks one heading from that file, or says none of them fit. If a parameter tip is only a short label, Gemma writes one sentence from that tip and the slider's real ends. A number that is not the low end, the high end, zero, or already written in the help is thrown away. The model does not get to choose the value for the shot.

**Two skill files.** A plain chat will wander off the manual. Each of those jobs is sent with a short instruction file. One file says: return a heading that is already in the list, or none. The other says: one sentence, using the help's own words and the slider ends, and do not invent a setting. The skill is how the model stays inside the page you already have.

**Temporal.** The heading pick is the step that can fail, because a local model can be busy or a request can time out. Temporal is an open-source workflow engine. Here it is one Python workflow that retries that pick. If Houdini quits while you are still on the node, the same card comes back. A new cook error starts a new card, because the problem in front of you changed.

**Entire.** Entire records the sessions from building the tool. Later I can search that history and ask why the shelf skips Gemma when a heading is already named. That record is for maintaining the project. It does not run when an artist clicks the shelf.

This is the path from the node you have selected to the window you keep open:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  activeNode["active network node"] --> wizard["houdini-wizard shelf"]
  wizard --> helpFile["installed help file"]
  helpFile --> gemma["Gemma picks one heading, or a short value line"]
  gemma --> quote["wizard quotes that help section"]
  gemma --> noMatch["no match lists headings you can open"]
  quote --> temporal["Temporal keeps this card"]
  noMatch --> temporal
  temporal --> updated["you update the node"]
```

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter

I kept hitting the same split while using Houdini. The manual that matches my install is already on the machine. The page a search sends me is often for another version. A hosted chat will happily describe a slider my node does not have, and sound sure about it.

That split is why the open tools here are doing the work, not sitting in a badge list.

Gemma is open-weight, and Ollama runs it beside Houdini. The scene does not have to be uploaded for a tooltip to be put into one clearer sentence. The words it may use still come from the help SideFX shipped with this build. Saketh Balijepalli wrote about a local assistant that is [not allowed to guess](https://dev.to/sakethbalijepalli/nannadesk-an-ai-assistant-for-my-dad-thats-not-allowed-to-guess-242l) on the subjects that matter. I wanted the same rule for a parameter value. If the manual already explains it, the model stays quiet.

The help files themselves are part of the install you already own. Quoting them means a beginner is reading the documentation for the Houdini they launched, not a write-up of a different one.

Temporal is open source, so the retry and the restored card are a workflow I can read, not a queue hidden in someone else's product. Entire is open source, so the reason a line of the shelf exists can be searched later, instead of living in a chat that disappeared.

None of those tools set the shot. You still change the parameter, the flag, and the wire. The window is there so the manual for the node you already have open is easier to use.

## Prize Categories

**Gemma**, because the model has two narrow reading jobs and is refused the rest. **Temporal**, because the heading pick can be retried and the card can come back. **Entire**, because the build keeps a record of why the shelf works this way.
